```go
package fsm

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/ecdsa"
	"encoding/json"
	"testing"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// Fixtures of the quarantine and rejected-part cleanup tests (Tasks 10 and
// 11). They build on tracksFSMQ: ownerFSMWithAuthority after the tracks
// activation, so indexer 1 (SNode s1, signer indexerSigner1) owns db.t
// and db.old, indexer 2 (SNode s2, signer indexerSigner2) owns db2.x, both
// SNodes and v1..v3 are Active, the cutover is the db2.x transition block
// (the sealed tip) and PromotionSeq is 0. Names end in Q so they stay clear
// of the other tasks' fixtures.

// tracksFSMQ is ownerFSMWithAuthority after the tracks activation signed by
// its authority (contract §7 A27): indexer 1 on s1 owns db.t and db.old,
// indexer 2 on s2 owns db2.x, the cutover is the db2.x transition block (the
// sealed tip) and PromotionSeq is 0. Task 6's tracksFSM numbers its second
// indexer 0 instead; these tests name indexer 2 throughout.
func tracksFSMQ(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := ownerFSMWithAuthority(t)
	mustApply(t, f, signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, tracksUpdateQ(t, f)))
	if !f.TracksActive() || f.st.Tracks == nil {
		t.Fatal("the tracks activation did not commit")
	}
	return f, a
}

// trackQ is indexer id's track state: the pointer into Tracks.Indexers that
// Apply writes through.
func trackQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, id uint64) *IndexerTrack {
	t.Helper()
	track := f.indexerTrackLocked(id)
	if track == nil {
		t.Fatalf("indexer %d has no track state", id)
	}
	return track
}

// tracksJSONQ is the track state as JSON; the snapshot document carries it
// only from v20 (Task 12) on.
func tracksJSONQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := json.Marshal(f.st.Tracks)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return b
}

// rejectQuarantineUnchanged is rejectConsensusUnchanged that also compares the
// track state, so a refused command cannot hide a change to it.
func rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t *testing.T, f *FSM, cmd wire.Command, reason string) {
	t.Helper()
	tracks := tracksJSONQ(t, f)
	rejectConsensusUnchanged(t, f, cmd, reason)
	if after := tracksJSONQ(t, f); !bytes.Equal(tracks, after) {
		t.Fatalf("a rejected command changed the track state: %s -> %s", tracks, after)
	}
}

// mustApplyUnchangedQ applies cmd, which must be accepted as a no-op: the
// snapshot and the track state stay byte-identical.
func mustApplyUnchangedQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, cmd wire.Command) {
	t.Helper()
	before, tracks := snapshotBytes(t, f), tracksJSONQ(t, f)
	mustApply(t, f, cmd)
	if !bytes.Equal(before, snapshotBytes(t, f)) || !bytes.Equal(tracks, tracksJSONQ(t, f)) {
		t.Fatal("an idempotent command changed replicated state")
	}
}

// quarantineAtQ is QuarantineIndexer{id, gen, reason} signed by signer under
// ctx.
func quarantineAtQ(t *testing.T, signer *authority.Signer, ctx authority.ConsensusContext, id, gen uint64, reason string) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.QuarantineIndexer{IndexerID: id, ExpectedGeneration: gen, Reason: reason}
	token, err := signer.SignQuarantineIndexerWithContext(cmd.Canonical(), ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cmd.AuthorityJWS = token
	return wire.Command{QuarantineIndexer: &cmd}
}

// quarantineQ is quarantineAtQ under f's current authority context.
func quarantineQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, id, gen uint64, reason string) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	return quarantineAtQ(t, signer, authorityContextFor(t, f), id, gen, reason)
}

// releaseAtQ is ReleaseIndexer{id, gen, acknowledged} signed by signer under
// ctx. The token covers the canonical form (sorted, unique) while the command
// carries acknowledged as given, so a test can commit a list the FSM must
// refuse under a valid signature.
func releaseAtQ(t *testing.T, signer *authority.Signer, ctx authority.ConsensusContext, id, gen uint64, acknowledged []uint64) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.ReleaseIndexer{IndexerID: id, ExpectedGeneration: gen, AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks: acknowledged}
	token, err := signer.SignReleaseIndexerWithContext(cmd.Canonical(), ctx)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cmd.AuthorityJWS = token
	return wire.Command{ReleaseIndexer: &cmd}
}

// releaseQ is releaseAtQ under f's current authority context.
func releaseQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, id, gen uint64, acknowledged ...uint64) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	return releaseAtQ(t, signer, authorityContextFor(t, f), id, gen, acknowledged)
}

// admitQ admits account's client seq into table under its live schema hash
// and returns the statement seq.
func admitQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, key *ecdsa.PrivateKey, account string, seq uint64, table string) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	live := f.st.TableRegistry.Live(table)
	if live == nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s is not registered", table)
	}
	r := submit(t, f, registryEnvelope(t, key, account, seq, table, live.SchemaHash))
	if r.Code != arbiter.AdmissionCodeAccepted {
		t.Fatalf("admit %s client seq %d = %+v", table, seq, r)
	}
	return r.StatementSeq
}

// partQ is one candidate part named all_1_0: hash in table/partition.
func partQ(table, partition, hash string) arbiter.CandidatePart {
	return arbiter.CandidatePart{TableID: table, PartitionID: partition, PartName: "all_1_0", PartRowLtHash: hash, RowCount: 1, Bytes: 32}
}

// signedRCQ is statement seq's result claim over parts from its bound source,
// signed by signer over the value Apply decodes.
func signedRCQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, seq uint64, parts ...arbiter.CandidatePart) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	ss := f.st.Statements[seq]
	if ss == nil {
		t.Fatalf("statement %d is unknown", seq)
	}
	rc := wire.RCFromPB(wire.RCToPB(arbiter.RCRecord{StatementID: ss.Env.StatementID, SourceNode: ss.SourceNode,
		SourceClaimRoot: "0xr00t", CandidateParts: parts}))
	jws, err := signer.SignSNodeMessage(authority.SNodeMessageResultClaim, messageContextFor(t, f), rc)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return wire.Command{RegisterRC: &wire.RegisterRC{RC: rc, SourceJWS: jws}}
}

// rejectBlockQ opens a challenge on blockSeq and resolves it Rejected.
func rejectBlockQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, blockSeq uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{OpenChallenge: &wire.OpenChallenge{BlockSeq: blockSeq, Reason: "verifier mismatch", OpenedBy: "v1"}})
	mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{ResolveChallenge: &wire.ResolveChallenge{BlockSeq: blockSeq, Verdict: wire.ChallengeVerdictRejected}})
}

// promotionQ is the next promotion of hashes in table/partition, signed by
// signer under f's current authority context.
func promotionQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, table, partition string, hashes ...string) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	promote := arbiter.PromoteSafePartition{TableID: table, PartitionID: partition, PromotionSeq: f.st.PromotionSeq + 1}
	for _, hash := range hashes {
		promote.CandidateParts = append(promote.CandidateParts, arbiter.PartRef{TableID: table, PartitionID: partition, PartRowLtHash: hash, PartName: "all_1_0"})
	}
	token, err := signer.SignPromotionWithContext(promote, authorityContextFor(t, f))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return wire.Command{RecordPromotionIssued: &wire.RecordPromotionIssued{Promote: promote, AuthorityJWS: token}}
}

// appliedAckQ is node's Applied acknowledgement of promotion seq over the one
// part hash in table/partition. The partition's base is empty, so the
// post-partition commitment is the part hash itself.
func appliedAckQ(node string, seq uint64, table, partition, hash string) arbiter.PromotionAck {
	return arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: node, PromotionSeq: seq, TableID: table, PartitionID: partition, PostPartitionCommitment: hash, Applied: true,
		Parts: []arbiter.SafePartMapping{{PartRowLtHash: hash, SafePartName: "all_9_9_0", PartPhysHash: "fixture-physical"}}}
}

// cleanupQ is the cleanup of promotion seq's hashes in table/partition,
// signed by signer under f's current authority context.
func cleanupQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, seq uint64, table, partition string, hashes ...string) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cleanup := arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{TableID: table, PartitionID: partition, PromotionSeq: seq}
	for _, hash := range hashes {
		cleanup.Parts = append(cleanup.Parts, arbiter.PartRef{TableID: table, PartitionID: partition, PartRowLtHash: hash, PartName: "all_1_0"})
	}
	token, err := signer.SignCleanupWithContext(cleanup, authorityContextFor(t, f))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return wire.Command{ScheduleUnsafeCleanup: &wire.ScheduleUnsafeCleanup{Cleanup: cleanup, AuthorityJWS: token}}
}

// tracksUpdateQ is f's next consensus update after the tracks activation:
// claimsUpdate carrying the committed si_indexers and verifiers, plus
// tracks_enabled, which every such update carries. The caller changes the
// authority set or max_writers, or the update is refused as a no-op.
func tracksUpdateQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM) arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate {
	t.Helper()
	u := claimsUpdate(t, f, f.st.Params.SIIndexers, f.st.Params.Verifiers)
	u.TracksEnabled = true
	return u
}

// quarantineEventsQ lists the BlockSeq of every EventIndexerQuarantineChanged
// in evs: 0 for a command, the rejected block for an automatic quarantine.
func quarantineEventsQ(evs []Event) []uint64 {
	var out []uint64
	for _, e := range evs {
		if e.Kind == EventIndexerQuarantineChanged {
			out = append(out, e.BlockSeq)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// suspendedWorkFSM is tracksFSMQ with one block of indexer 2 holding statement
// A (part pA of db2.x/p1) and statement B (part pB of db2.x/p2): promotion 1
// of pA acknowledged by s2 and its cleanup scheduled, promotion 2 of pB
// issued and not acknowledged, so pA is a promoted unsafe part. That is the
// work a stuck track holds. Issuance and cleanup scheduling read neither
// statement status nor verification (promotionCoveredStatementSeqs,
// applyScheduleUnsafeCleanup), so the block is not verified first. It returns
// the FSM, the network authority, pA and pB.
func suspendedWorkFSM(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, string, string) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	pA, pB := lthashHex("rowA"), lthashHex("rowB")
	seqA := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	seqB := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 2, "db2.x")
	mustSeal(t, f)
	second := indexerSigner2(t)
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, second, seqA, partQ("db2.x", "p1", pA)))
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, second, seqB, partQ("db2.x", "p2", pB)))
	mustApply(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, a, "db2.x", "p1", pA))
	mustApply(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, a, "db2.x", "p2", pB))
	mustApply(t, f, sourceAck(t, f, second, appliedAckQ("s2", 1, "db2.x", "p1", pA)))
	mustApply(t, f, cleanupQ(t, f, a, 1, "db2.x", "p1", pA))
	if pp := f.st.PendingPromotions[2]; pp == nil || pp.Acked || f.st.PendingCleanups[1] == nil {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: promotions %v, cleanups %v", f.st.PendingPromotions, f.st.PendingCleanups)
	}
	return f, a, pA, pB
}
```

Create `fsm/quarantine_test.go`:

```go
package fsm

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// TestQuarantineCommandsAreRefusedBeforeTheTracksActivation: before the
// activation both commands are refused first, with no state change, as a
// voter that predates Raft tags 36 and 37 refuses them at decode; with and
// without the signed-claims activation.
func TestQuarantineCommandsAreRefusedBeforeTheTracksActivation(t *testing.T) {
	claims, a := ownerFSMWithAuthority(t)
	legacy := newTestFSM(t)
	legacyCtx := authority.ConsensusContext{NetworkID: legacy.st.Params.NetworkID, GenesisSnapshotID: mustGenesisID(t, legacy)}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		f    *FSM
		cmd  wire.Command
	}{
		{"quarantine after signed claims", claims, quarantineQ(t, claims, a, 2, 0, "operator hold")},
		{"release after signed claims", claims, releaseQ(t, claims, a, 2, 1)},
		{"quarantine without a registry", legacy, quarantineAtQ(t, a, legacyCtx, 1, 0, "operator hold")},
		{"release without a registry", legacy, releaseAtQ(t, a, legacyCtx, 1, 1, nil)},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, tc.f, tc.cmd, quarantineBeforeTracksReason)
			if tc.f.st.Tracks != nil {
				t.Fatal("a refused command created track state")
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestQuarantineCommandsNeedTheCurrentAuthorityContext (contract §3.5): the
// token is an authority token over exactly this command, bound to the
// current {network, genesis, epoch}; the indexer must be enrolled and a
// quarantine needs a reason.
func TestQuarantineCommandsNeedTheCurrentAuthorityContext(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	ctx := authorityContextFor(t, f)
	previous := ctx
	previous.AuthorityEpoch--
	network := ctx
	network.NetworkID = "another-network"
	genesis := ctx
	genesis.GenesisSnapshotID = "0x" + strings.Repeat("ab", 32)
	other := quarantineQ(t, f, a, 1, 0, "operator hold")
	other.QuarantineIndexer.IndexerID = 2
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		cmd    wire.Command
		reason string
	}{
		{"not an authority", quarantineAtQ(t, indexerSigner1(t), ctx, 2, 0, "operator hold"), "quarantine indexer 2: authority"},
		{"previous epoch", quarantineAtQ(t, a, previous, 2, 0, "operator hold"), "quarantine indexer 2: authority"},
		{"another network", quarantineAtQ(t, a, network, 2, 0, "operator hold"), "quarantine indexer 2: authority"},
		{"another genesis", quarantineAtQ(t, a, genesis, 2, 0, "operator hold"), "quarantine indexer 2: authority"},
		{"another command", other, "quarantine indexer 2: authority"},
		{"unsigned", wire.Command{QuarantineIndexer: &wire.QuarantineIndexer{IndexerID: 2, Reason: "operator hold"}}, "quarantine indexer 2: authority"},
		{"not enrolled", quarantineQ(t, f, a, 9, 0, "operator hold"), "indexer 9 is not an si_indexers entry"},
		{"no reason", wire.Command{QuarantineIndexer: &wire.QuarantineIndexer{IndexerID: 2, Reason: "  ", AuthorityJWS: "h.p.s"}}, "quarantine indexer 2: reason must be non-empty"},
		{"release by a non-authority", releaseAtQ(t, indexerSigner1(t), ctx, 2, 0, nil), "release indexer 2: authority"},
		{"release of a past epoch", releaseAtQ(t, a, previous, 2, 0, nil), "release indexer 2: authority"},
		{"release not enrolled", releaseQ(t, f, a, 9, 0), "indexer 9 is not an si_indexers entry"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) { rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, tc.cmd, tc.reason) })
	}
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold"))
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); !track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineReason != "operator hold" || track.QuarantineGeneration != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
}

// TestQuarantineAndReleaseMoveTheGeneration (spec §7.4): every applied
// command increments the generation, bumps the registry once and wakes the
// leader; quarantining a quarantined track and releasing a released one are
// refused; the other track is untouched.
func TestQuarantineAndReleaseMoveTheGeneration(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	ch := make(chan Event, 16)
	f.notify = ch
	version := f.st.TableRegistry.Version
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold"))
	track := trackQ(t, f, 2)
	if !track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineReason != "operator hold" || track.QuarantineGeneration != 1 || f.st.TableRegistry.Version != version+1 {
		t.Fatalf("after the quarantine: track %+v, registry version %d (was %d)", track, f.st.TableRegistry.Version, version)
	}
	if got := quarantineEventsQ(drain(ch)); !slices.Equal(got, []uint64{0}) {
		t.Fatalf("quarantine events = %v, want one", got)
	}
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 1, "again"), "indexer 2 is already quarantined")
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1))
	track = trackQ(t, f, 2)
	if track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineReason != "" || track.QuarantineGeneration != 2 || f.st.TableRegistry.Version != version+2 {
		t.Fatalf("after the release: track %+v, registry version %d (was %d)", track, f.st.TableRegistry.Version, version)
	}
	if got := quarantineEventsQ(drain(ch)); !slices.Equal(got, []uint64{0}) {
		t.Fatalf("release events = %v, want one", got)
	}
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 2), "indexer 2 is not quarantined")
	if other := trackQ(t, f, 1); other.Quarantined || other.QuarantineGeneration != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("track 1 = %+v", other)
	}
}

// TestQuarantineReplayAfterReleaseIsRefused (Review Focus 4): an old
// quarantine replayed after the release that ended it names a past
// generation and is refused.
func TestQuarantineReplayAfterReleaseIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	quarantine := quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold")
	mustApply(t, f, quarantine)
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1))
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, quarantine, "expected_generation 0 differs from quarantine generation 2 of indexer 2")
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineGeneration != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
}

// TestReleaseReplayAfterLaterQuarantineIsRefused (Review Focus 4): an old
// release replayed against a later quarantine names a past generation and is
// refused, so the later quarantine stands.
func TestReleaseReplayAfterLaterQuarantineIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "first hold"))
	release := releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1)
	mustApply(t, f, release)
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 2, "second hold"))
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, release, "expected_generation 1 differs from quarantine generation 3 of indexer 2")
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); !track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineReason != "second hold" || track.QuarantineGeneration != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
}

// TestReleaseSignedBeforeAutomaticQuarantineIsRefused (Review Focus 4, spec
// §7.5): a release signed while the track held no rejected block is refused
// once a Rejected verdict has quarantined the track again, so the operator
// reviews the rejection; the release that names the new generation must
// acknowledge the block.
func TestReleaseSignedBeforeAutomaticQuarantineIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	block := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold"))
	early := releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1)
	rejectBlockQ(t, f, block)
	track := trackQ(t, f, 2)
	if !track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineGeneration != 2 || !slices.Equal(track.Rejected, []uint64{block}) ||
		track.QuarantineReason != fmt.Sprintf("block %d rejected", block) {
		t.Fatalf("after the Rejected verdict: track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, early, "expected_generation 1 differs from quarantine generation 2 of indexer 2")
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 2), fmt.Sprintf("release must acknowledge exactly the rejected blocks [%d]", block))
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 2, block))
	track = trackQ(t, f, 2)
	if track.Quarantined || track.Rejected != nil || !slices.Equal(track.Acknowledged, []uint64{block}) || track.QuarantineGeneration != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("after the release: track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
}

// TestRejectedBlockQuarantinesItsTrack (spec §7.5): a Rejected verdict on a
// block of a track records the block, quarantines the track with the block
// as reason, increments the generation, bumps the registry and wakes the
// leader; a verdict that changes no statement does nothing, and a
// source-favoured verdict on the other track's block quarantines nothing.
func TestRejectedBlockQuarantinesItsTrack(t *testing.T) {
	f, _ := tracksFSMQ(t)
	ch := make(chan Event, 16)
	f.notify = ch
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	block := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	drain(ch)
	version := f.st.TableRegistry.Version
	rejectBlockQ(t, f, block)
	track := trackQ(t, f, 2)
	if !track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineReason != fmt.Sprintf("block %d rejected", block) || track.QuarantineGeneration != 1 ||
		!slices.Equal(track.Rejected, []uint64{block}) || track.Acknowledged != nil {
		t.Fatalf("track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
	if got := quarantineEventsQ(drain(ch)); !slices.Equal(got, []uint64{block}) {
		t.Fatalf("quarantine events = %v, want block %d", got, block)
	}
	view, ok := f.TableRegistryView()
	if !ok || !slices.Equal(view.QuarantinedIndexers, []uint64{2}) || view.Version != version+1 {
		t.Fatalf("registry view: quarantined %v, version %d (was %d)", view.QuarantinedIndexers, view.Version, version)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{ResolveChallenge: &wire.ResolveChallenge{BlockSeq: block, Verdict: wire.ChallengeVerdictRejected}})
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); track.QuarantineGeneration != 1 || f.st.TableRegistry.Version != version+1 {
		t.Fatalf("a verdict that changed nothing moved track 2: %+v, version %d", track, f.st.TableRegistry.Version)
	}
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 2, "db.t")
	other := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{OpenChallenge: &wire.OpenChallenge{BlockSeq: other, Reason: "audit", OpenedBy: "v1"}})
	mustApply(t, f, wire.Command{ResolveChallenge: &wire.ResolveChallenge{BlockSeq: other, Verdict: wire.ChallengeVerdictSafe}})
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 1); track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineGeneration != 0 || track.Rejected != nil {
		t.Fatalf("track 1 = %+v", track)
	}
}

// TestRejectedBlockBeforeTheTracksActivationIsUnchanged: before the
// activation a Rejected verdict only rejects the statements, as in stage 1;
// no track state appears and the registry is not bumped.
func TestRejectedBlockBeforeTheTracksActivationIsUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
	f := ownerFSM(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	seq := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	block := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	version := f.st.TableRegistry.Version
	rejectBlockQ(t, f, block)
	if f.st.Statements[seq].Status != StatusRejected || f.st.Tracks != nil || f.st.TableRegistry.Version != version || f.st.Blocks[block-1].Track != nil {
		t.Fatalf("status %v, tracks %+v, registry version %d (was %d)", f.st.Statements[seq].Status, f.st.Tracks, f.st.TableRegistry.Version, version)
	}
	if view, ok := f.TableRegistryView(); !ok || view.QuarantinedIndexers != nil {
		t.Fatalf("pre-activation view carries quarantined indexers %v", view.QuarantinedIndexers)
	}
}

// TestReleaseMustAcknowledgeExactlyTheRejectedBlocks (spec §7.5, contract
// §3.5): the committed list must be exactly the track's unacknowledged
// rejected blocks, sorted and unique; the release moves them to Acknowledged,
// after which each counts as passed for its track and for the global prefix
// (clarification C3).
func TestReleaseMustAcknowledgeExactlyTheRejectedBlocks(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	first := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 2, "db2.x")
	second := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	rejectBlockQ(t, f, first)
	rejectBlockQ(t, f, second)
	track := trackQ(t, f, 2)
	if !slices.Equal(track.Rejected, []uint64{first, second}) || track.QuarantineGeneration != 2 || track.QuarantineReason != fmt.Sprintf("block %d rejected", second) {
		t.Fatalf("track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
	want := fmt.Sprintf("release must acknowledge exactly the rejected blocks [%d %d]", first, second)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name         string
		acknowledged []uint64
	}{
		{"none", nil},
		{"a subset", []uint64{first}},
		{"unsorted", []uint64{second, first}},
		{"duplicated", []uint64{first, first, second}},
		{"an extra block", []uint64{first, second, second + 1}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, releaseAtQ(t, a, authorityContextFor(t, f), 2, 2, tc.acknowledged), want)
		})
	}
	if f.blockPassedLocked(first) || f.blockPassedLocked(second) || safePrefixLocked(f) != first-1 {
		t.Fatalf("unacknowledged rejected blocks passed: prefix %d", safePrefixLocked(f))
	}
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 2, first, second))
	track = trackQ(t, f, 2)
	if track.Quarantined || track.Rejected != nil || !slices.Equal(track.Acknowledged, []uint64{first, second}) || track.QuarantineGeneration != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("after the release: track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
	if !f.blockPassedLocked(first) || !f.blockPassedLocked(second) || f.trackPrefixLocked(2) != second || safePrefixLocked(f) != second {
		t.Fatalf("acknowledged blocks: track prefix %d, global prefix %d, want %d", f.trackPrefixLocked(2), safePrefixLocked(f), second)
	}
}

// TestRegistryViewCarriesTheQuarantinedSet (contract §3.5): the view lists
// the quarantined indexers ascending, nil when none, detached from state;
// every command bumps the version once.
func TestRegistryViewCarriesTheQuarantinedSet(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	view := func() TableRegistryView {
		t.Helper()
		v, ok := f.TableRegistryView()
		if !ok {
			t.Fatal("registry view unavailable")
		}
		return v
	}
	start := view()
	if start.QuarantinedIndexers != nil {
		t.Fatalf("quarantined at the activation: %v", start.QuarantinedIndexers)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "hold two"))
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 1, 0, "hold one"))
	held := view()
	if !slices.Equal(held.QuarantinedIndexers, []uint64{1, 2}) || held.Version != start.Version+2 {
		t.Fatalf("view: quarantined %v, version %d (was %d)", held.QuarantinedIndexers, held.Version, start.Version)
	}
	held.QuarantinedIndexers[0] = 99
	if got := view().QuarantinedIndexers; !slices.Equal(got, []uint64{1, 2}) {
		t.Fatalf("the view aliases state: %v", got)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 1, 1))
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1))
	if end := view(); end.QuarantinedIndexers != nil || end.Version != start.Version+4 {
		t.Fatalf("view after the releases: quarantined %v, version %d (was %d)", end.QuarantinedIndexers, end.Version, start.Version)
	}
}
```

```go
package fsm

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// Quarantine and release (housegate spec 2026-10-10 §7.4-§7.5, contract
// §3.5). A track is quarantined by an authority-signed QuarantineIndexer, or
// automatically when a challenge resolves one of its blocks as Rejected, and
// released by an authority-signed ReleaseIndexer that acknowledges exactly the
// track's unacknowledged rejected blocks. Both commands live outside
// ConsensusParamsUpdate, so the drain gate never blocks them, and both are
// bound to the track's quarantine generation, which every applied quarantine,
// release and automatic quarantine increments. Neither command advances the
// consensus epoch, so the generation, not the token, is what refuses a signed
// command replayed within one epoch.

// quarantineBeforeTracksReason refuses both commands before the tracks
// activation, with no state change. A voter built before Raft tags 36 and 37
// refuses them at decode, so a stage-2 voter refuses them too; the leader
// proposes neither before the activation.
const quarantineBeforeTracksReason = "quarantine requires the tracks activation"

func (f *FSM) applyQuarantineIndexer(c *wire.QuarantineIndexer) any {
	if !f.tracksActiveLocked() {
		return Rejected{Reason: quarantineBeforeTracksReason}
	}
	// Restore refuses a quarantined track without a reason (contract §3.7),
	// so Apply never creates one (amendment A8, proposed as G5-2).
	shape := ""
	if strings.TrimSpace(c.Reason) == "" {
		shape = "reason must be non-empty"
	}
	track, reason := f.trackCommandLocked("quarantine", c.IndexerID, c.ExpectedGeneration, shape,
		func(v *authority.Validator, ctx authority.ConsensusContext) error {
			_, err := v.VerifyQuarantineIndexer(c.Canonical(), c.AuthorityJWS, ctx)
			return err
		})
	if reason != "" {
		return Rejected{Reason: reason}
	}
	if track.Quarantined {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("indexer %d is already quarantined", c.IndexerID)}
	}
	track.Quarantined = true
	track.QuarantineReason = c.Reason
	f.quarantineChangedLocked(track, 0)
	return Applied{}
}

func (f *FSM) applyReleaseIndexer(c *wire.ReleaseIndexer) any {
	if !f.tracksActiveLocked() {
		return Rejected{Reason: quarantineBeforeTracksReason}
	}
	track, reason := f.trackCommandLocked("release", c.IndexerID, c.ExpectedGeneration, "",
		func(v *authority.Validator, ctx authority.ConsensusContext) error {
			_, err := v.VerifyReleaseIndexer(c.Canonical(), c.AuthorityJWS, ctx)
			return err
		})
	if reason != "" {
		return Rejected{Reason: reason}
	}
	if !track.Quarantined {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("indexer %d is not quarantined", c.IndexerID)}
	}
	// The committed list itself, not its canonical form, must be exactly the
	// track's unacknowledged rejected blocks: sorted, unique, none missing
	// and none added (spec 2026-10-10 §7.5).
	if !slices.Equal(c.AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks, track.Rejected) {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("release must acknowledge exactly the rejected blocks %v", track.Rejected)}
	}
	for _, block := range track.Rejected {
		track.Acknowledged = insertSortedUnique(track.Acknowledged, block)
	}
	track.Rejected = nil
	track.Quarantined = false
	track.QuarantineReason = ""
	f.quarantineChangedLocked(track, 0)
	return Applied{}
}

// trackCommandLocked runs the checks QuarantineIndexer and ReleaseIndexer
// share after the activation check, in the contract's order: an si_indexers
// entry for the id, then shape (a refusal the caller derived from the command
// alone, empty when none), then the authority token, verified like
// evictNodeRefusalLocked under the exact current {network, genesis, epoch}
// with no clock (only the RPC enforces token age), then the generation.
func (f *FSM) trackCommandLocked(kind string, id, expectedGeneration uint64, shape string, verify func(*authority.Validator, authority.ConsensusContext) error) (*IndexerTrack, string) {
	if _, ok := f.siIndexerLocked(id); !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("indexer %d is not an si_indexers entry", id)
	}
	if shape != "" {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("%s indexer %d: %s", kind, id, shape)
	}
	track := f.indexerTrackLocked(id)
	if track == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("indexer %d has no track state", id)
	}
	genesisID, err := f.genesisSnapshotIDLocked()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("%s indexer %d: %v", kind, id, err)
	}
	validator := &authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: authorityAddressSet(f.st.Params.AuthorityAddresses)}
	ctx := authority.ConsensusContext{NetworkID: f.st.Params.NetworkID, GenesisSnapshotID: genesisID, AuthorityEpoch: f.st.ConsensusEpoch}
	if err := verify(validator, ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("%s indexer %d: authority: %v", kind, id, err)
	}
	if expectedGeneration != track.QuarantineGeneration {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("expected_generation %d differs from quarantine generation %d of indexer %d", expectedGeneration, track.QuarantineGeneration, id)
	}
	return track, ""
}

// quarantineRejectedBlockLocked is the automatic quarantine (spec 2026-10-10
// §7.5). After the tracks activation, a Rejected verdict that changed at
// least one statement of a block with a track adds the block to the track's
// Rejected list and quarantines the track with reason "block <n> rejected",
// incrementing the generation whether or not the track was already
// quarantined, so a release signed before the rejection is refused and the
// operator reviews it first. Blocks sealed before the activation carry no
// track and keep stage 1's behaviour.
func (f *FSM) quarantineRejectedBlockLocked(blockSeq uint64) {
	if !f.tracksActiveLocked() {
		return
	}
	id, ok := f.blockTrackLocked(blockSeq)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	track := f.indexerTrackLocked(id)
	if track == nil {
		return
	}
	track.Rejected = insertSortedUnique(track.Rejected, blockSeq)
	track.Quarantined = true
	track.QuarantineReason = fmt.Sprintf("block %d rejected", blockSeq)
	f.quarantineChangedLocked(track, blockSeq)
}

// quarantineChangedLocked finishes every applied quarantine, release and
// automatic quarantine (spec 2026-10-10 §7.4): the generation increments,
// the registry is bumped once (its view carries the quarantined set) and
// EventIndexerQuarantineChanged wakes the leader, whose next pass withholds
// or re-dispatches the track's work. blockSeq names the rejected block of an
// automatic quarantine and is 0 otherwise. The activation needs si_indexers,
// which needs the registry, so State.TableRegistry is non-nil here.
func (f *FSM) quarantineChangedLocked(track *IndexerTrack, blockSeq uint64) {
	track.QuarantineGeneration++
	f.registryChangedLocked(f.st.TableRegistry)
	f.emit(Event{Kind: EventIndexerQuarantineChanged, BlockSeq: blockSeq})
}

// quarantinedIndexersLocked lists the quarantined indexers in ascending id
// order (Tracks.Indexers is sorted by id), nil when none; the registry view
// serves it as quarantined_indexers.
func (f *FSM) quarantinedIndexersLocked() []uint64 {
	if f.st.Tracks == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []uint64
	for _, track := range f.st.Tracks.Indexers {
		if track.Quarantined {
			out = append(out, track.IndexerID)
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
// TestQuarantinedAdmissionIsUnspent (spec §7.4, contract §3.5): a quarantined
// indexer's table answers INDEXER_QUARANTINED with state unchanged, so the
// client_seq stays unspent and the same statement is admitted after the
// release; the other indexer's tables are unaffected.
func TestQuarantinedAdmissionIsUnspent(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold"))
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	env := registryEnvelope(t, key, account, 1, "db2.x", f.st.TableRegistry.Live("db2.x").SchemaHash)
	coord := env.StatementID.Coord()
	root, next := f.st.SpentIDs.Root(), f.st.NextStatementSeq
	before := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	r := submit(t, f, env)
	if r.Code != arbiter.AdmissionCodeIndexerQuarantined || r.Message != "storage-integrity indexer 2 is quarantined" || r.StatementSeq != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("submit = %+v, want INDEXER_QUARANTINED", r)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(before, snapshotBytes(t, f)) {
		t.Fatal("INDEXER_QUARANTINED changed replicated state")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(root, f.st.SpentIDs.Root()) || f.st.SpentIDs.Status(coord) != accumulator.StatusFresh || f.st.NextStatementSeq != next {
		t.Fatal("INDEXER_QUARANTINED spent the client_seq")
	}
	if _, indexed := f.st.ByStatementID[env.StatementID.Flat()]; indexed {
		t.Fatal("a refused statement was indexed")
	}
	if r := submit(t, f, registryEnvelope(t, key, account, 2, "db.t", genesisSchemaHash(t, f))); r.Code != arbiter.AdmissionCodeAccepted {
		t.Fatalf("db.t while indexer 2 is quarantined = %+v", r)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1))
	if r := submit(t, f, env); r.Code != arbiter.AdmissionCodeAccepted || f.st.Statements[r.StatementSeq].SourceNode != "s2" {
		t.Fatalf("the same statement after the release = %+v", r)
	}
}

// TestQuarantineAnswersBeforeTheSourceCheck (clarification C9): a quarantined
// indexer whose SNode is down answers the non-retryable INDEXER_QUARANTINED,
// never the retryable SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; a duplicate client_seq and a
// refused target still answer first.
func TestQuarantineAnswersBeforeTheSourceCheck(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	hash := f.st.TableRegistry.Live("db2.x").SchemaHash
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold"))
	f.st.Nodes["s2"].Status = NodeSyncing
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		env  arbiter.StatementEnvelope
		code arbiter.AdmissionCode
	}{
		{"a duplicate client_seq", registryEnvelope(t, key, account, 1, "db2.x", hash), arbiter.AdmissionCodeDuplicateClientSeq},
		{"a schema mismatch", registryEnvelope(t, key, account, 2, "db2.x", "0x"+strings.Repeat("44", 32)), arbiter.AdmissionCodeSchemaNotAllowed},
		{"a source that is down", registryEnvelope(t, key, account, 2, "db2.x", hash), arbiter.AdmissionCodeIndexerQuarantined},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if r := submit(t, f, tc.env); r.Code != tc.code {
				t.Fatalf("submit = %+v, want code %d", r, tc.code)
			}
		})
	}
}

// refusedOwnerSwitchQuarantineSubtest is the quarantine case of Task 7's
// TestRefusedOwnerSwitchSealsNothing (Review Focus 1): indexer 1's statement
// holds the open block and indexer 2 is quarantined, so indexer 2's statement
// is refused with INDEXER_QUARANTINED before any seal is prepared: no block
// is sealed and the state is byte-identical.
func refusedOwnerSwitchQuarantineSubtest(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db.t")
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold"))
	env := registryEnvelope(t, key, account, 2, "db2.x", f.st.TableRegistry.Live("db2.x").SchemaHash)
	blocks := len(f.st.Blocks)
	before := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	if r := submit(t, f, env); r.Code != arbiter.AdmissionCodeIndexerQuarantined {
		t.Fatalf("submit = %+v, want INDEXER_QUARANTINED", r)
	}
	if len(f.st.Blocks) != blocks || !bytes.Equal(before, snapshotBytes(t, f)) {
		t.Fatal("a refused owner switch sealed a block or changed state")
	}
	if owner := f.st.OpenBlock.Owner; owner == nil || *owner != 1 || len(f.st.OpenBlock.StatementSeqs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("open block = %+v, want indexer 1's single statement", f.st.OpenBlock)
	}
}

// TestQuarantinedTrackIssuesNoNewWork (clarification C8): while a track is
// quarantined no promotion is issued and no cleanup is scheduled for it; the
// other track keeps issuing; after the release both are accepted again.
func TestQuarantinedTrackIssuesNoNewWork(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	pA, pB, pE := lthashHex("rowA"), lthashHex("rowB"), lthashHex("rowE")
	seqA := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	seqB := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 2, "db2.x")
	mustSeal(t, f)
	seqE := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 3, "db.t")
	mustSeal(t, f)
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, indexerSigner2(t), seqA, partQ("db2.x", "p1", pA)))
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, indexerSigner2(t), seqB, partQ("db2.x", "p2", pB)))
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, indexerSigner1(t), seqE, partQ("db.t", "p0", pE)))
	mustApply(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, a, "db2.x", "p1", pA))
	mustApply(t, f, sourceAck(t, f, indexerSigner2(t), appliedAckQ("s2", 1, "db2.x", "p1", pA)))
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "operator hold"))
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, a, "db2.x", "p2", pB), "indexer 2 is quarantined; no new promotion is issued")
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, cleanupQ(t, f, a, 1, "db2.x", "p1", pA), "indexer 2 is quarantined; no new cleanup is scheduled")
	mustApply(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, a, "db.t", "p0", pE))
	if f.st.PromotionSeq != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("PromotionSeq = %d, want indexer 1's promotion 2", f.st.PromotionSeq)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1))
	mustApply(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, a, "db2.x", "p2", pB))
	mustApply(t, f, cleanupQ(t, f, a, 1, "db2.x", "p1", pA))
	if f.st.PromotionSeq != 3 || f.st.PendingCleanups[1] == nil {
		t.Fatalf("after the release: PromotionSeq %d, cleanups %v", f.st.PromotionSeq, f.st.PendingCleanups)
	}
}

// TestQuarantinedTrackStillTakesLateAcknowledgements (spec §7.4): a
// quarantine cancels nothing, so an acknowledgement the source sends while
// its track is quarantined (for work it received before) is recorded as
// usual.
func TestQuarantinedTrackStillTakesLateAcknowledgements(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, _, pB := suspendedWorkFSM(t)
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "stuck source"))
	second := indexerSigner2(t)
	mustApply(t, f, sourceAck(t, f, second, appliedAckQ("s2", 2, "db2.x", "p2", pB)))
	mustApply(t, f, sourceCleanupAck(t, f, second, arbiter.CleanupAck{NodeID: "s2", PromotionSeq: 1, TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p1"}))
	p1 := arbiter.TablePartition{TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p1"}
	p2 := arbiter.TablePartition{TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p2"}
	if !f.st.PendingPromotions[2].Acked || f.st.PendingCleanups[1] != nil || f.st.PromotedUnsafe[p1] != nil || !f.st.PromotedUnsafe[p2][pB] {
		t.Fatalf("late acknowledgements: promotion 2 %+v, cleanups %v, promoted unsafe %v", f.st.PendingPromotions[2], f.st.PendingCleanups, f.st.PromotedUnsafe)
	}
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); !track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineGeneration != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
}

// TestWorkSetOmitsAQuarantinedTracksWork (clarification C8): a quarantined
// track's issued promotion and scheduled cleanup stay recorded but leave the
// WorkSet, so nothing is dispatched; the release brings both back for the
// orchestrator's resend paths.
func TestWorkSetOmitsAQuarantinedTracksWork(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, pA, pB := suspendedWorkFSM(t)
	requireSuspendedWork := func(t *testing.T, listed bool) {
		t.Helper()
		ws := mustWorkSet(t, f)
		issued := len(ws.IssuedUnacked) == 1 && ws.IssuedUnacked[0].Promote.PromotionSeq == 2 &&
			len(ws.IssuedUnacked[0].Promote.CandidateParts) == 1 && ws.IssuedUnacked[0].Promote.CandidateParts[0].PartRowLtHash == pB
		scheduled := len(ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups) == 1 && ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups[0].PromotionSeq == 1 &&
			len(ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups[0].Cleanup.Parts) == 1 && ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups[0].Cleanup.Parts[0].PartRowLtHash == pA
		empty := len(ws.IssuedUnacked) == 0 && len(ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups) == 0
		if (listed && !(issued && scheduled)) || (!listed && !empty) {
			t.Fatalf("issued %+v, scheduled cleanups %+v (want listed: %v)", ws.IssuedUnacked, ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups, listed)
		}
	}
	requireSuspendedWork(t, true)
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "stuck source"))
	requireSuspendedWork(t, false)
	if f.st.PendingPromotions[2].Acked || f.st.PendingCleanups[1] == nil {
		t.Fatal("the quarantine cancelled recorded work")
	}
	flagged := false
	for _, tw := range mustWorkSet(t, f).Tracks {
		if tw.IndexerID == 2 {
			flagged = tw.Quarantined && tw.QuarantineGeneration == 1
		}
	}
	if !flagged {
		t.Fatalf("WorkSet.Tracks = %+v, want indexer 2 quarantined at generation 1", mustWorkSet(t, f).Tracks)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1))
	requireSuspendedWork(t, true)
}

// TestDrainGateSkipsAQuarantinedTrack (Review Focus 5, spec §7.4): while the
// stuck track 2 holds an unacknowledged promotion, a pending cleanup and a
// promoted unsafe part, every consensus update is refused. Once it is
// quarantined an authority rotation passes and the work stays recorded;
// track 1's unacknowledged promotion still holds the next update; after the
// release the suspended work is acknowledged under the new authority's epoch.
func TestDrainGateSkipsAQuarantinedTrack(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, pA, pB := suspendedWorkFSM(t)
	b, _ := authorityFixture(t)
	rotate := tracksUpdateQ(t, f)
	rotate.AuthorityAddresses = []string{b.Address()}
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, rotate), "consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged")
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "stuck source"))
	epoch := f.st.ConsensusEpoch
	mustApply(t, f, signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, rotate))
	if f.st.ConsensusEpoch != epoch+1 || !f.AuthorityAllowed(b.Address()) {
		t.Fatalf("rotation: epoch %d (was %d)", f.st.ConsensusEpoch, epoch)
	}
	p1 := arbiter.TablePartition{TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p1"}
	if f.st.PendingPromotions[2].Acked || f.st.PendingCleanups[1] == nil || !f.st.PromotedUnsafe[p1][pA] {
		t.Fatal("the update cancelled the quarantined track's suspended work")
	}
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	pE := lthashHex("rowE")
	seqE := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db.t")
	mustSeal(t, f)
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, indexerSigner1(t), seqE, partQ("db.t", "p0", pE)))
	mustApply(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, b, "db.t", "p0", pE))
	bump := func() wire.Command {
		u := tracksUpdateQ(t, f)
		u.MaxWriters++
		return signedConsensusUpdate(t, b, u)
	}
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, bump(), "consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged")
	notApplied := arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: "s1", PromotionSeq: 3, TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p0", Applied: false, Detail: "base CAS failed"}
	mustApply(t, f, sourceAck(t, f, indexerSigner1(t), notApplied))
	mustApply(t, f, bump())
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, b, 2, 1))
	second := indexerSigner2(t)
	mustApply(t, f, sourceAck(t, f, second, appliedAckQ("s2", 2, "db2.x", "p2", pB)))
	mustApply(t, f, sourceCleanupAck(t, f, second, arbiter.CleanupAck{NodeID: "s2", PromotionSeq: 1, TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p1"}))
	if !f.st.PendingPromotions[2].Acked || f.st.PendingCleanups[1] != nil || f.st.PromotedUnsafe[p1] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("suspended work after the release: promotion 2 %+v, cleanups %v, promoted unsafe %v", f.st.PendingPromotions[2], f.st.PendingCleanups, f.st.PromotedUnsafe)
	}
}

// TestHistoryAcceptsQuarantinedWorkFromAnEarlierEpoch (proposed amendment
// G5-1): restore's consensus-history audit accepts an unacknowledged
// promotion and a pending cleanup of a quarantined track issued before the
// consensus update the drain gate let pass, so a snapshot taken then is not
// refused.
func TestHistoryAcceptsQuarantinedWorkFromAnEarlierEpoch(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, _, _ := suspendedWorkFSM(t)
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 0, "stuck source"))
	u := tracksUpdateQ(t, f)
	u.MaxWriters++
	mustApply(t, f, signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, u))
	if f.st.PendingPromotions[2].AuthorityEpoch >= f.st.ConsensusEpoch {
		t.Fatal("fixture: the suspended promotion must predate the update")
	}
	if err := validateConsensusHistory(f.st, nil, f.st.BootstrapParams); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("restore would refuse the quarantined track's suspended work: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestTracksWorkEpochFloor: the floor is the first epoch whose parameters
// carry tracks_enabled; without one there is none.
func TestTracksWorkEpochFloor(t *testing.T) {
	off, on := Params{}, Params{TracksEnabled: true}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		epochs []Params
		floor  uint64
		ok     bool
	}{
		{"never enabled", []Params{off, off, off}, 0, false},
		{"enabled by the first update", []Params{off, on}, 1, true},
		{"enabled by the third update", []Params{off, off, off, on, on}, 3, true},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if floor, ok := tracksWorkEpochFloor(tc.epochs); floor != tc.floor || ok != tc.ok {
				t.Fatalf("tracksWorkEpochFloor = %d, %v; want %d, %v", floor, ok, tc.floor, tc.ok)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

Append to `fsm/quarantine.go`:

```go
// drainGateRefusalLocked is the consensus-update drain gate: every promotion
// acknowledged, every cleanup acknowledged and every promoted unsafe part
// cleaned. Before the tracks activation it is exactly that, over all work.
// After it a quarantined track's work does not count (spec 2026-10-10 §7.4):
// its pending promotions and cleanups stay recorded, undispatched, and must
// not block the governance that might release it. A promotion and the
// cleanup that names it resolve their track through promotionTrackLocked, a
// promoted unsafe part through manifestTableOwnerLocked; work whose track does
// not resolve counts. The refusals keep today's strings and order, so the
// result does not depend on map order.
func (f *FSM) drainGateRefusalLocked() string {
	tracks := f.tracksActiveLocked()
	quarantined := func(id uint64, ok bool) bool { return ok && f.indexerQuarantinedLocked(id) }
	for seq, pending := range f.st.PendingPromotions {
		if pending == nil || pending.Acked {
			continue
		}
		if tracks && quarantined(f.promotionTrackLocked(seq)) {
			continue
		}
		return "consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged"
	}
	for seq := range f.st.PendingCleanups {
		if tracks && quarantined(f.promotionTrackLocked(seq)) {
			continue
		}
		return "consensus update requires all cleanup commands to be acknowledged"
	}
	for tp, parts := range f.st.PromotedUnsafe {
		if tracks && quarantined(f.manifestTableOwnerLocked(tp.TableID)) {
			continue
		}
		for _, pending := range parts {
			if pending {
				return "consensus update requires all promoted unsafe parts to be cleaned"
			}
		}
	}
	return ""
}
```

```go
// tracksWorkEpochFloor is the first authority epoch whose parameters carry
// tracks_enabled, and ok is false while no committed update set it. From that
// epoch on a consensus update may pass while a quarantined track holds work
// issued in an earlier epoch (spec 2026-10-10 §7.4).
func tracksWorkEpochFloor(paramsByEpoch []Params) (uint64, bool) {
	for epoch, params := range paramsByEpoch {
		if params.TracksEnabled {
			return uint64(epoch), true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}
```

Notes:
- **Keyed by (block, table, partition), never by promotion.** A rejected statement's parts were never promoted (clarification C4), so the work lives in `Tracks.RejectedParts`, kept sorted by `compareRejectedPartitions`, with its scheduled command, token and epoch inside the entry. It never enters `PendingCleanups` or `CleanupAudits`: both are keyed by promotion sequence, and the restore audit (`fsm/consensus_history.go:100-135`) would read a `promotion_seq 0` entry as a promotion's cleanup. Task 12 persists and validates `RejectedParts` (v20).
- **Only a release creates the work.** `applyReleaseIndexer` computes it with `rejectedPartitionsLocked` before its first mutation: per acknowledged block, the candidate parts of the Rejected statements' bound RCs still in `UnpromotedParts`, grouped by partition, sorted by `PartRowLtHash`, part names kept (the SNode refuses a cleanup part without one, `arbiter-core:snode/cleanup.go:29-31`). A part a promotion already took is a promoted unsafe part and is cleaned by that promotion's own cleanup. An incomplete block refuses the release with state unchanged. So no command carries `rejected_block_seq` before the tracks activation, and Apply refuses one that does, first and with no state change, as a voter that predates the field refuses it at decode.
- **Exact parts, idempotent re-schedule.** The block, partition and exact parts fix the whole command, so a second schedule of a scheduled partition is the same command and a no-op that keeps the first token. The authority token is verified like every cleanup's (`verifyCurrentAuthority` over `authority.CleanupCommandHash`, which covers `rejected_block_seq`).
- **The source acknowledges.** The expected source is the bound `SourceNode` every Rejected statement of the block shares (after the activation a block holds one owner's statements), the same answer `RejectedCleanupSource` gives the orchestrator; the acknowledgement must name it and carry its `SNodeMessageCleanupAck` signature over the decoded acknowledgement, `rejected_block_seq` included. An acknowledgement for a partition that is not recorded is an idempotent no-op, exactly like one for a promotion cleanup that is not pending; one for a recorded partition that was never scheduled is refused, since its source cannot have received the command.
- **A quarantined track neither schedules nor dispatches** rejected-part cleanups (`WorkSet` omits them, `applyScheduleUnsafeCleanup` refuses), and the drain gate skips its rejected partitions; a released track's rejected partitions hold the gate until acknowledged, like any other cleanup.
- **Orchestrator.** `ws.RejectedUncleaned` goes through `scheduleCleanup` (authority-signed, proposed, then streamed with the signed token) and `ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups` through `streamCleanup` (re-signed under the current authority context on every pass); both keep their logic and their warn logs only gain `rejected_block_seq`. Only routing changes: `streamCleanupSigned` sends through `cleanupTargets`, which routes a rejected-part cleanup to `FSM.RejectedCleanupSource` and every other cleanup through `promotionTargets` exactly as before. `RejectedBlockSeq` is 0 on every cleanup before the activation, so dispatch is byte-identical.
- **Data plane.** Task 5's SNode echoes `rejected_block_seq` in its signed `CleanupAck`, and Task 13's gateway refuses that field before the activation and forwards it afterwards.

Create `fsm/rejected_cleanup_test.go`:

```go
package fsm

import (
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// rejectedHashesQ names the part hashes rejectedPartsFSM's statements claim.
type rejectedHashesQ struct{ A, B, C, D string }

// rejectedPartsFSM is tracksFSMQ with one block of indexer 2 holding three
// statements of db2.x, rejected by a challenge, which quarantines indexer 2
// at generation 1: statement A claims pA in p1, pB in p2 and pD in p3, and its
// promotion of pD was issued and acknowledged before the challenge (issuance
// does not read statement status); statement C claims pC in p1; statement N
// bound no claim. It returns the FSM, the network authority, the block and
// the hashes.
func rejectedPartsFSM(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer, uint64, rejectedHashesQ) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	h := rejectedHashesQ{A: lthashHex("rowA"), B: lthashHex("rowB"), C: lthashHex("rowC"), D: lthashHex("rowD")}
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	seqA := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	seqC := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 2, "db2.x")
	admitQ(t, f, key, account, 3, "db2.x")
	block := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	second := indexerSigner2(t)
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, second, seqA, partQ("db2.x", "p1", h.A), partQ("db2.x", "p2", h.B), partQ("db2.x", "p3", h.D)))
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, second, seqC, partQ("db2.x", "p1", h.C)))
	mustApply(t, f, promotionQ(t, f, a, "db2.x", "p3", h.D))
	mustApply(t, f, sourceAck(t, f, second, appliedAckQ("s2", 1, "db2.x", "p3", h.D)))
	rejectBlockQ(t, f, block)
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); !track.Quarantined || track.QuarantineGeneration != 1 || !slices.Equal(track.Rejected, []uint64{block}) {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
	return f, a, block, h
}

// partRefQ is the PartRef partQ's candidate part becomes in a rejected
// partition.
func partRefQ(table, partition, hash string) arbiter.PartRef {
	return arbiter.PartRef{TableID: table, PartitionID: partition, PartRowLtHash: hash, PartName: "all_1_0"}
}

// sortedPartRefsQ sorts parts by PartRowLtHash, RejectedPartition.Parts'
// order.
func sortedPartRefsQ(parts ...arbiter.PartRef) []arbiter.PartRef {
	slices.SortFunc(parts, func(x, y arbiter.PartRef) int { return strings.Compare(x.PartRowLtHash, y.PartRowLtHash) })
	return parts
}

// rejectedCleanupsQ are the cleanups of the partitions a release of
// rejectedPartsFSM's block records: p1 (pA, pC) and p2 (pB).
func rejectedCleanupsQ(block uint64, h rejectedHashesQ) (p1, p2 arbiter.UnsafeCleanup) {
	p1 = arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p1", RejectedBlockSeq: block,
		Parts: sortedPartRefsQ(partRefQ("db2.x", "p1", h.A), partRefQ("db2.x", "p1", h.C))}
	p2 = arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p2", RejectedBlockSeq: block,
		Parts: []arbiter.PartRef{partRefQ("db2.x", "p2", h.B)}}
	return p1, p2
}

// rejectedCleanupQ is cl signed by signer under f's current authority
// context.
func rejectedCleanupQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, cl arbiter.UnsafeCleanup) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	token, err := signer.SignCleanupWithContext(cl, authorityContextFor(t, f))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return wire.Command{ScheduleUnsafeCleanup: &wire.ScheduleUnsafeCleanup{Cleanup: cl, AuthorityJWS: token}}
}

// rejectedAckQ is node's acknowledgement of the rejected-part cleanup cl,
// signed by signer.
func rejectedAckQ(t *testing.T, f *FSM, signer *authority.Signer, node string, cl arbiter.UnsafeCleanup) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	return sourceCleanupAck(t, f, signer, arbiter.CleanupAck{NodeID: node, TableID: cl.TableID, PartitionID: cl.PartitionID, RejectedBlockSeq: cl.RejectedBlockSeq})
}

// rejectedPartitionQ is the recorded partition (block, table, partition), or
// nil.
func rejectedPartitionQ(f *FSM, block uint64, table, partition string) *RejectedPartition {
	_, rp := f.rejectedPartitionLocked(block, table, partition)
	return rp
}

// TestRejectedCleanupFieldsAreRefusedBeforeTheTracksActivation: before the
// activation a cleanup or an acknowledgement carrying rejected_block_seq is
// refused first with no state change, as a voter that predates the field
// refuses it at decode, and the WorkSet has no rejected-part rows.
func TestRejectedCleanupFieldsAreRefusedBeforeTheTracksActivation(t *testing.T) {
	claims, a := ownerFSMWithAuthority(t)
	cleanup := arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p1", RejectedBlockSeq: 1,
		Parts: []arbiter.PartRef{partRefQ("db2.x", "p1", lthashHex("rowA"))}}
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, claims, rejectedCleanupQ(t, claims, a, cleanup), rejectedCleanupBeforeTracksReason)
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, claims, rejectedAckQ(t, claims, indexerSigner2(t), "s2", cleanup), rejectedCleanupBeforeTracksReason)
	legacy := newTestFSM(t)
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, legacy, wire.Command{RecordCleanupAck: &wire.RecordCleanupAck{
		Ack: arbiter.CleanupAck{NodeID: "s1", TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p0", RejectedBlockSeq: 1}}}, rejectedCleanupBeforeTracksReason)
	if ws := mustWorkSet(t, claims); ws.RejectedUncleaned != nil || ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups != nil {
		t.Fatalf("pre-activation WorkSet has rejected-part rows: %+v / %+v", ws.RejectedUncleaned, ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups)
	}
}

// TestRejectedBlockIsCleanedAndPassed walks spec §7.5 end to end: a Rejected
// verdict quarantines the block's track; a release acknowledging the block
// records, per partition, the parts its Rejected statements still hold
// unpromoted; each partition's cleanup is scheduled and acknowledged by the
// block's source, which removes it; and the block counts as passed for its
// track and for the global prefix (clarification C3) from the release on.
func TestRejectedBlockIsCleanedAndPassed(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, block, h := rejectedPartsFSM(t)
	cutover := block - 1
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); track.QuarantineReason != fmt.Sprintf("block %d rejected", block) {
		t.Fatalf("after the Rejected verdict: track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
	if f.blockPassedLocked(block) || f.trackPrefixLocked(2) != cutover || safePrefixLocked(f) != cutover {
		t.Fatal("an unacknowledged rejected block passed")
	}
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1, block))
	p1, p2 := rejectedCleanupsQ(block, h)
	want := []RejectedPartition{
		{BlockSeq: block, TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p1", Parts: p1.Parts},
		{BlockSeq: block, TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p2", Parts: p2.Parts},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts, want) {
		t.Fatalf("recorded rejected parts = %+v, want %+v (pD was promoted before the challenge, statement N bound no claim)", f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts, want)
	}
	if !f.blockPassedLocked(block) || f.trackPrefixLocked(2) != block || safePrefixLocked(f) != block || f.trackPrefixLocked(1) != cutover {
		t.Fatalf("after the release: track prefixes %d/%d, global prefix %d", f.trackPrefixLocked(1), f.trackPrefixLocked(2), safePrefixLocked(f))
	}
	ws := mustWorkSet(t, f)
	if len(ws.RejectedUncleaned) != 2 || len(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("after the release: %+v / %+v", ws.RejectedUncleaned, ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups)
	}
	for _, row := range ws.RejectedUncleaned {
		mustApply(t, f, rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, row.Cleanup))
	}
	ws = mustWorkSet(t, f)
	if len(ws.RejectedUncleaned) != 0 || len(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("after scheduling: %+v / %+v", ws.RejectedUncleaned, ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups)
	}
	for _, row := range ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups {
		mustApply(t, f, rejectedAckQ(t, f, indexerSigner2(t), "s2", row.Cleanup))
	}
	if f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rejected parts after the acknowledgements = %+v", f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts)
	}
	if ws := mustWorkSet(t, f); ws.RejectedUncleaned != nil || ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rows after the acknowledgements: %+v / %+v", ws.RejectedUncleaned, ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups)
	}
	if !f.blockPassedLocked(block) || safePrefixLocked(f) != block {
		t.Fatal("the cleaned block stopped passing")
	}
	if !f.st.PromotedUnsafe[arbiter.TablePartition{TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p3"}][h.D] {
		t.Fatal("the rejected-part cleanup touched a promoted part, which promotion 1's own cleanup owns")
	}
}

// TestReleaseOfAnIncompleteRejectedBlockIsRefused: the release computes its
// cleanup work before its first mutation, so a rejected block whose
// statement list is short (local corruption, Spec P D1) refuses it with state
// unchanged rather than leave parts behind.
func TestReleaseOfAnIncompleteRejectedBlockIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, block, _ := rejectedPartsFSM(t)
	statements := f.blockStatements(block)
	delete(f.st.Statements, statements[len(statements)-1].Seq) // synthesized corruption
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1, block), fmt.Sprintf("release indexer 2: block %d is unknown or incomplete", block))
	if track := trackQ(t, f, 2); !track.Quarantined || track.Acknowledged != nil {
		t.Fatalf("track 2 = %+v", track)
	}
}

// TestRejectedCleanupScheduleRules (contract §3.6): a rejected-part cleanup
// names no promotion, is authority-signed like every cleanup, and names a
// recorded partition with exactly its parts; it records the command, token
// and epoch; an identical re-schedule is a no-op; a quarantined track
// schedules nothing new.
func TestRejectedCleanupScheduleRules(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, block, h := rejectedPartsFSM(t)
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1, block))
	p1, p2 := rejectedCleanupsQ(block, h)
	withPromotion := p2
	withPromotion.PromotionSeq = 1
	unrecorded := p2
	unrecorded.PartitionID = "p9"
	unrecorded.Parts = []arbiter.PartRef{partRefQ("db2.x", "p9", h.B)}
	otherBlock := p2
	otherBlock.RejectedBlockSeq = block + 1
	subset := p1
	subset.Parts = p1.Parts[:1]
	reordered := p1
	reordered.Parts = []arbiter.PartRef{p1.Parts[1], p1.Parts[0]}
	extra := p2
	extra.Parts = append(slices.Clone(p2.Parts), partRefQ("db2.x", "p2", lthashHex("rowZ")))
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		cmd    wire.Command
		reason string
	}{
		{"a promotion_seq", rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, withPromotion), "rejected-part cleanup must carry promotion_seq 0"},
		{"an unrecorded partition", rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, unrecorded), fmt.Sprintf("no rejected parts of block %d are recorded in db2.x/p9", block)},
		{"another block", rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, otherBlock), fmt.Sprintf("no rejected parts of block %d are recorded in db2.x/p2", block+1)},
		{"a subset of the parts", rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, subset), "the parts differ from the rejected parts of block"},
		{"reordered parts", rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, reordered), "the parts differ from the rejected parts of block"},
		{"an extra part", rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, extra), "the parts differ from the rejected parts of block"},
		{"not an authority", rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, indexerSigner1(t), p2), "authority token"},
		{"unsigned", wire.Command{ScheduleUnsafeCleanup: &wire.ScheduleUnsafeCleanup{Cleanup: p2}}, "authority token"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) { rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, tc.cmd, tc.reason) })
	}
	mustApply(t, f, rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, p2))
	rp := rejectedPartitionQ(f, block, "db2.x", "p2")
	if rp == nil || rp.Scheduled == nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(*rp.Scheduled, p2) || rp.AuthorityJWS == "" || rp.AuthorityEpoch != f.st.ConsensusEpoch {
		t.Fatalf("scheduled partition = %+v", rp)
	}
	token, err := a.SignCleanupWithContextAt(p2, authorityContextFor(t, f), 1)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	mustApplyUnchangedQ(t, f, wire.Command{ScheduleUnsafeCleanup: &wire.ScheduleUnsafeCleanup{Cleanup: p2, AuthorityJWS: token}})
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 2, "cleanup review"))
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, p1), "indexer 2 is quarantined; no new cleanup is scheduled")
}

// TestRejectedCleanupAckRules (contract §3.6): only the shared source of the
// block's Rejected statements acknowledges a scheduled rejected-part cleanup,
// with its signature over the acknowledgement including rejected_block_seq;
// the acknowledgement removes the partition; one for a partition that is not
// recorded is an idempotent no-op.
func TestRejectedCleanupAckRules(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, block, h := rejectedPartsFSM(t)
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1, block))
	_, p2 := rejectedCleanupsQ(block, h)
	founder, second := indexerSigner1(t), indexerSigner2(t)
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, rejectedAckQ(t, f, second, "s2", p2), fmt.Sprintf("the rejected parts of block %d in db2.x/p2 are not scheduled", block))
	mustApply(t, f, rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, p2))
	ack := arbiter.CleanupAck{NodeID: "s2", TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p2", RejectedBlockSeq: block}
	withPromotion := ack
	withPromotion.PromotionSeq = 1
	unbound := sourceCleanupAck(t, f, second, arbiter.CleanupAck{NodeID: "s2", TableID: "db2.x", PartitionID: "p2"})
	unbound.RecordCleanupAck.Ack.RejectedBlockSeq = block
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		cmd    wire.Command
		reason string
	}{
		{"another node", rejectedAckQ(t, f, founder, "s1", p2), fmt.Sprintf("cleanup_ack from s1: only the source s2 may acknowledge the rejected parts of block %d", block)},
		{"unsigned", wire.Command{RecordCleanupAck: &wire.RecordCleanupAck{Ack: ack}}, "snode signature"},
		{"another key", sourceCleanupAck(t, f, founder, ack), "snode signature"},
		{"a signature without the field", unbound, "snode signature"},
		{"a promotion_seq", sourceCleanupAck(t, f, second, withPromotion), "rejected-part cleanup ack must carry promotion_seq 0"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) { rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, tc.cmd, tc.reason) })
	}
	unrecorded := ack
	unrecorded.PartitionID = "p9"
	mustApplyUnchangedQ(t, f, sourceCleanupAck(t, f, second, unrecorded))
	mustApply(t, f, rejectedAckQ(t, f, second, "s2", p2))
	if rejectedPartitionQ(f, block, "db2.x", "p2") != nil || rejectedPartitionQ(f, block, "db2.x", "p1") == nil {
		t.Fatalf("rejected parts after the acknowledgement = %+v", f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts)
	}
	mustApplyUnchangedQ(t, f, rejectedAckQ(t, f, second, "s2", p2))
}

// TestRejectedCleanupSourceIsTheBlocksSource (contract §3.6): the routing
// read names the shared bound source of the block's Rejected statements and
// refuses a block without one.
func TestRejectedCleanupSourceIsTheBlocksSource(t *testing.T) {
	f, _, block, _ := rejectedPartsFSM(t)
	if node, err := f.RejectedCleanupSource(block); node != "s2" || err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RejectedCleanupSource(%d) = %q, %v; want s2", block, node, err)
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		block  uint64
		reason string
	}{
		{"the cutover block", block - 1, fmt.Sprintf("block %d holds no rejected statement", block-1)},
		{"an unknown block", block + 7, fmt.Sprintf("block %d is unknown or incomplete", block+7)},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if _, err := f.RejectedCleanupSource(tc.block); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.reason) {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, want %q", err, tc.reason)
			}
		})
	}
	f.blockStatements(block)[1].SourceNode = "s1" // synthesized corruption: two sources in one block
	if _, err := f.RejectedCleanupSource(block); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "bound to different sources (s2, s1)") {
		t.Fatalf("disagreeing sources: err = %v", err)
	}
}

// TestWorkSetListsRejectedCleanupWork (contract §3.6, clarification C8): the
// WorkSet lists recorded partitions to schedule and scheduled ones to resend,
// detached from state, both omitted while the track is quarantined and back
// after the release.
func TestWorkSetListsRejectedCleanupWork(t *testing.T) {
	f, a, block, h := rejectedPartsFSM(t)
	if ws := mustWorkSet(t, f); ws.RejectedUncleaned != nil || ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rows before the release: %+v / %+v", ws.RejectedUncleaned, ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups)
	}
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1, block))
	p1, p2 := rejectedCleanupsQ(block, h)
	requireRows := func(t *testing.T, unscheduled, scheduled []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup) {
		t.Helper()
		ws := mustWorkSet(t, f)
		cleanups := func(rows []CleanupWork) []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup {
			var out []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup
			for _, row := range rows {
				if row.PromotionSeq != 0 {
					t.Fatalf("a rejected-part row names promotion %d", row.PromotionSeq)
				}
				out = append(out, row.Cleanup)
			}
			return out
		}
		if u, s := cleanups(ws.RejectedUncleaned), cleanups(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups); !reflect.DeepEqual(u, unscheduled) || !reflect.DeepEqual(s, scheduled) {
			t.Fatalf("unscheduled %+v, scheduled %+v; want %+v, %+v", u, s, unscheduled, scheduled)
		}
	}
	requireRows(t, []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{p1, p2}, nil)
	mustApply(t, f, rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, p1))
	requireRows(t, []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{p2}, []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{p1})
	ws := mustWorkSet(t, f)
	ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups[0].Cleanup.Parts[0].PartName = "mutated"
	ws.RejectedUncleaned[0].Cleanup.Parts[0].PartName = "mutated"
	if rp := rejectedPartitionQ(f, block, "db2.x", "p1"); rp.Parts[0].PartName != "all_1_0" || rp.Scheduled.Parts[0].PartName != "all_1_0" {
		t.Fatal("a WorkSet row aliases the recorded parts")
	}
	if rp := rejectedPartitionQ(f, block, "db2.x", "p2"); rp.Parts[0].PartName != "all_1_0" {
		t.Fatal("a WorkSet row aliases the recorded parts")
	}
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 2, "cleanup review"))
	requireRows(t, nil, nil)
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 3))
	requireRows(t, []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{p2}, []arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{p1})
}

// TestRejectedPartitionGatesConsensusUpdates (contract §3.5): a rejected
// partition of a track that is not quarantined holds the drain gate until its
// source acknowledges the cleanup; while the track is quarantined it does
// not.
func TestRejectedPartitionGatesConsensusUpdates(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := tracksFSMQ(t)
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	seq := admitQ(t, f, key, account, 1, "db2.x")
	block := mustSeal(t, f).BlockSeq
	mustApply(t, f, signedRCQ(t, f, indexerSigner2(t), seq, partQ("db2.x", "p1", lthashHex("rowA"))))
	rejectBlockQ(t, f, block)
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 1, block))
	update := func() wire.Command {
		u := tracksUpdateQ(t, f)
		u.MaxWriters++
		return signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, u)
	}
	const held = "consensus update requires all rejected-part cleanups to be acknowledged"
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, update(), held)
	mustApply(t, f, quarantineQ(t, f, a, 2, 2, "cleanup source down"))
	mustApply(t, f, update())
	mustApply(t, f, releaseQ(t, f, a, 2, 3))
	cleanup := mustWorkSet(t, f).RejectedUncleaned[0].Cleanup
	mustApply(t, f, rejectedCleanupQ(t, f, a, cleanup))
	rejectQuarantineUnchanged(t, f, update(), held)
	mustApply(t, f, rejectedAckQ(t, f, indexerSigner2(t), "s2", cleanup))
	mustApply(t, f, update())
}
```
