Create `fsm/rejected_cleanup.go`:

```go
package fsm

import (
	"cmp"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// Rejected-part cleanup (housegate spec 2026-10-10 §7.5, clarification C4,
// contract §3.6). A rejected statement's candidate parts were never promoted,
// so no promotion sequence keys their cleanup. A release that acknowledges
// block b records, per partition, the parts b's Rejected statements still
// hold unpromoted (Tracks.RejectedParts); the leader schedules each through
// ScheduleUnsafeCleanup{promotion_seq: 0, rejected_block_seq: b} and streams
// it to b's source, whose signed CleanupAck echoing rejected_block_seq
// removes the partition. Only a release creates such work, so no command
// carries rejected_block_seq before the tracks activation.

// rejectedCleanupBeforeTracksReason refuses a cleanup or an acknowledgement
// carrying rejected_block_seq before the tracks activation, first and with
// no state change, as a voter that predates the field refuses it at decode.
const rejectedCleanupBeforeTracksReason = "rejected-part cleanup requires the tracks activation"

// compareRejectedPartitions orders Tracks.RejectedParts by (block, table,
// partition), the key every rejected-part cleanup and acknowledgement names.
func compareRejectedPartitions(a, b RejectedPartition) int {
	return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(a.BlockSeq, b.BlockSeq), strings.Compare(a.TableID, b.TableID), strings.Compare(a.PartitionID, b.PartitionID))
}

// rejectedPartitionLocked returns the recorded partition (block, table,
// partition) and its index in Tracks.RejectedParts, or -1 and nil when none
// is recorded.
func (f *FSM) rejectedPartitionLocked(block uint64, table, partition string) (int, *RejectedPartition) {
	if f.st.Tracks == nil {
		return -1, nil
	}
	key := RejectedPartition{BlockSeq: block, TableID: table, PartitionID: partition}
	i, found := slices.BinarySearchFunc(f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts, key, compareRejectedPartitions)
	if !found {
		return -1, nil
	}
	return i, &f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts[i]
}

// rejectedPartitionsLocked computes the cleanup work a release acknowledging
// blocks creates: per block, one RejectedPartition per partition in which a
// Rejected statement still holds a candidate part of its bound RC in
// UnpromotedParts, with the parts sorted by PartRowLtHash and their names
// kept (an SNode drops a part by name). A part a promotion already took is a
// promoted unsafe part, cleaned by that promotion's own cleanup. It only
// reads, so the release refuses before its first mutation when a block is
// incomplete: a short statement list would leave parts behind (Spec P D1).
func (f *FSM) rejectedPartitionsLocked(blocks []uint64) ([]RejectedPartition, string) {
	var out []RejectedPartition
	for _, block := range blocks {
		statements, ok := f.blockStatementsComplete(block)
		if !ok {
			return nil, fmt.Sprintf("block %d is unknown or incomplete", block)
		}
		parts := map[arbiter.TablePartition]map[string]arbiter.PartRef{}
		for _, ss := range statements {
			if ss.Status != StatusRejected || ss.RC == nil {
				continue
			}
			for _, cp := range ss.RC.CandidateParts {
				if !ss.UnpromotedParts[cp.PartRowLtHash] {
					continue
				}
				tp := arbiter.TablePartition{TableID: cp.TableID, PartitionID: cp.PartitionID}
				if parts[tp] == nil {
					parts[tp] = map[string]arbiter.PartRef{}
				}
				parts[tp][cp.PartRowLtHash] = arbiter.PartRef{TableID: cp.TableID, PartitionID: cp.PartitionID,
					PartRowLtHash: cp.PartRowLtHash, PartName: cp.PartName}
			}
		}
		partitions := slices.Collect(maps.Keys(parts))
		sortPartitions(partitions)
		for _, tp := range partitions {
			refs := slices.Collect(maps.Values(parts[tp]))
			slices.SortFunc(refs, func(x, y arbiter.PartRef) int { return strings.Compare(x.PartRowLtHash, y.PartRowLtHash) })
			out = append(out, RejectedPartition{BlockSeq: block, TableID: tp.TableID, PartitionID: tp.PartitionID, Parts: refs})
		}
	}
	return out, ""
}

// recordRejectedPartitionsLocked adds a release's rejected partitions to
// Tracks.RejectedParts and keeps it sorted. A block is acknowledged once (its
// statements are then Rejected or Safe, which no challenge reopens), so no
// key is recorded twice.
func (f *FSM) recordRejectedPartitionsLocked(parts []RejectedPartition) {
	if len(parts) == 0 {
		return
	}
	f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts = append(f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts, parts...)
	slices.SortFunc(f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts, compareRejectedPartitions)
}

// rejectedSourceLocked is the node that must acknowledge block blockSeq's
// rejected-part cleanups: the bound SourceNode every Rejected statement of
// the block shares. After the tracks activation a block holds one owner's
// statements, all bound to that owner's SNode; reason names why there is no
// such node.
func (f *FSM) rejectedSourceLocked(blockSeq uint64) (node, reason string) {
	statements, ok := f.blockStatementsComplete(blockSeq)
	if !ok {
		return "", fmt.Sprintf("block %d is unknown or incomplete", blockSeq)
	}
	for _, ss := range statements {
		if ss.Status != StatusRejected {
			continue
		}
		switch {
		case ss.SourceNode == "":
			return "", fmt.Sprintf("block %d holds rejected statement %d, which has no bound source", blockSeq, ss.Seq)
		case node == "":
			node = ss.SourceNode
		case ss.SourceNode != node:
			return "", fmt.Sprintf("block %d holds rejected statements bound to different sources (%s, %s)", blockSeq, node, ss.SourceNode)
		}
	}
	if node == "" {
		return "", fmt.Sprintf("block %d holds no rejected statement", blockSeq)
	}
	return node, ""
}

// RejectedCleanupSource is where the orchestrator sends block blockSeq's
// rejected-part cleanups (contract §3.6): the node whose signed
// acknowledgement applyRecordCleanupAck requires.
func (f *FSM) RejectedCleanupSource(blockSeq uint64) (string, error) {
	f.mu.RLock()
	defer f.mu.RUnlock()
	node, reason := f.rejectedSourceLocked(blockSeq)
	if reason != "" {
		return "", errors.New(reason)
	}
	return node, nil
}

// scheduleRejectedCleanupLocked records the authority-signed cleanup of one
// rejected partition, after applyScheduleUnsafeCleanup's shape and authority
// checks. The partition must be recorded, its track not quarantined
// (clarification C8), and the command must name exactly its parts; the
// block, partition and parts then fix the whole command, so a second
// schedule of a scheduled partition is the same command and a no-op.
func (f *FSM) scheduleRejectedCleanupLocked(c *wire.ScheduleUnsafeCleanup) any {
	cl := c.Cleanup
	_, rp := f.rejectedPartitionLocked(cl.RejectedBlockSeq, cl.TableID, cl.PartitionID)
	if rp == nil {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("schedule cleanup: no rejected parts of block %d are recorded in %s/%s", cl.RejectedBlockSeq, cl.TableID, cl.PartitionID)}
	}
	if track, ok := f.blockTrackLocked(cl.RejectedBlockSeq); ok && f.indexerQuarantinedLocked(track) {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("indexer %d is quarantined; no new cleanup is scheduled", track)}
	}
	if !slices.Equal(rp.Parts, cl.Parts) {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("schedule cleanup: the parts differ from the rejected parts of block %d in %s/%s", cl.RejectedBlockSeq, cl.TableID, cl.PartitionID)}
	}
	if rp.Scheduled != nil {
		return Applied{} // the same cleanup again: idempotent (§10.3), the first token stays
	}
	scheduled := cl
	scheduled.Parts = clonePartRefs(cl.Parts)
	rp.Scheduled = &scheduled
	rp.AuthorityJWS = c.AuthorityJWS
	rp.AuthorityEpoch = f.st.ConsensusEpoch
	f.emit(Event{Kind: EventCleanupScheduled, BlockSeq: cl.RejectedBlockSeq})
	return Applied{}
}

// recordRejectedCleanupAckLocked takes the acknowledgement of a rejected-part
// cleanup: after the tracks activation, naming no promotion, for a recorded
// and scheduled partition, from the block's source and signed by it over the
// acknowledgement, rejected_block_seq included. It removes the partition. An
// acknowledgement for a partition that is not recorded is an idempotent no-op,
// like one for a promotion cleanup that is not pending.
func (f *FSM) recordRejectedCleanupAckLocked(c *wire.RecordCleanupAck) any {
	ack := c.Ack
	if !f.tracksActiveLocked() {
		return Rejected{Reason: rejectedCleanupBeforeTracksReason}
	}
	if ack.PromotionSeq != 0 {
		return Rejected{Reason: "rejected-part cleanup ack must carry promotion_seq 0"}
	}
	i, rp := f.rejectedPartitionLocked(ack.RejectedBlockSeq, ack.TableID, ack.PartitionID)
	if rp == nil {
		return Applied{} // already cleaned or never recorded: idempotent (§10.3)
	}
	if rp.Scheduled == nil {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("cleanup ack: the rejected parts of block %d in %s/%s are not scheduled", ack.RejectedBlockSeq, ack.TableID, ack.PartitionID)}
	}
	kind := authority.SNodeMessageCleanupAck
	expected, reason := f.rejectedSourceLocked(ack.RejectedBlockSeq)
	if reason != "" {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s", kind, reason)}
	}
	if ack.NodeID != expected {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("%s from %s: only the source %s may acknowledge the rejected parts of block %d", kind, ack.NodeID, expected, ack.RejectedBlockSeq)}
	}
	if err := f.snodeSignatureLocked(kind, expected, ack, c.SourceJWS); err != nil {
		return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("%s from %s: %v", kind, ack.NodeID, err)}
	}
	f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts = slices.Delete(f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts, i, i+1)
	if len(f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts) == 0 {
		f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts = nil
	}
	f.emit(Event{Kind: EventCleanupAcked, BlockSeq: ack.RejectedBlockSeq})
	return Applied{}
}

// rejectedCleanupWorkLocked lists, in RejectedParts order, the recorded
// rejected-part cleanups of tracks that are not quarantined (clarification
// C8): the unscheduled ones to schedule and the scheduled ones to resend,
// each a detached copy. Both are nil before the tracks activation.
func (f *FSM) rejectedCleanupWorkLocked() (unscheduled, scheduled []CleanupWork) {
	if f.st.Tracks == nil {
		return nil, nil
	}
	for _, rp := range f.st.Tracks.RejectedParts {
		if track, ok := f.blockTrackLocked(rp.BlockSeq); ok && f.indexerQuarantinedLocked(track) {
			continue
		}
		if rp.Scheduled == nil {
			unscheduled = append(unscheduled, CleanupWork{Cleanup: arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{TableID: rp.TableID, PartitionID: rp.PartitionID,
				RejectedBlockSeq: rp.BlockSeq, Parts: clonePartRefs(rp.Parts)}})
			continue
		}
		cl := *rp.Scheduled
		cl.Parts = clonePartRefs(rp.Scheduled.Parts)
		scheduled = append(scheduled, CleanupWork{Cleanup: cl})
	}
	return unscheduled, scheduled
}
```

`fsm/apply.go` — `applyScheduleUnsafeCleanup` (as Task 10 left it) becomes:

```go
func (f *FSM) applyScheduleUnsafeCleanup(c *wire.ScheduleUnsafeCleanup) any {
	// A rejected-part cleanup (clarification C4) exists only after the
	// tracks activation and never names a promotion.
	if c.Cleanup.RejectedBlockSeq != 0 {
		if !f.tracksActiveLocked() {
			return Rejected{Reason: rejectedCleanupBeforeTracksReason}
		}
		if c.Cleanup.PromotionSeq != 0 {
			return Rejected{Reason: "rejected-part cleanup must carry promotion_seq 0"}
		}
	}
	for _, pr := range c.Cleanup.Parts {
		if pr.TableID != c.Cleanup.TableID || pr.PartitionID != c.Cleanup.PartitionID {
			return Rejected{Reason: "cleanup part outside the command's partition (§8.1 single-partition command)"}
		}
	}
	if hasNULIDs(c.Cleanup.TableID, c.Cleanup.PartitionID) {
		return Rejected{Reason: "NUL byte in table/partition id"}
	}
	wantHash, err := authority.CleanupCommandHash(c.Cleanup)
	if err != nil {
		return Rejected{Reason: "hash cleanup command: " + err.Error()}
	}
	if err := f.verifyCurrentAuthority(c.AuthorityJWS, wantHash); err != nil {
		return Rejected{Reason: err.Error()}
	}
	if c.Cleanup.RejectedBlockSeq != 0 {
		return f.scheduleRejectedCleanupLocked(c)
	}
	// After the activation only the promotion's source may acknowledge a
	// cleanup, so a cleanup whose promotion has no resolvable source could
	// never be acknowledged and would block every later consensus update.
	if f.signedClaimsActiveLocked() {
		if _, reason := f.expectedSourceLocked(c.Cleanup.PromotionSeq); reason != "" {
			return Rejected{Reason: "schedule cleanup: " + reason}
		}
	}
	// A quarantined track issues no new work (clarification C8): its
	// promotion's cleanup waits for the release, which brings it back into
	// the WorkSet.
	if f.tracksActiveLocked() {
		if track, ok := f.promotionTrackLocked(c.Cleanup.PromotionSeq); ok && f.indexerQuarantinedLocked(track) {
			return Rejected{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("indexer %d is quarantined; no new cleanup is scheduled", track)}
		}
	}
	if pending, dup := f.st.PendingCleanups[c.Cleanup.PromotionSeq]; dup {
		previousHash, err := authority.CleanupCommandHash(*pending)
		if err != nil || previousHash != wantHash {
			return Rejected{Reason: "cleanup sequence already has a different pending command"}
		}
		if !f.st.LegacyCleanupProofs[c.Cleanup.PromotionSeq] {
			return Applied{} // idempotent re-schedule already has an audit proof
		}
	}
	cl := c.Cleanup
	f.st.PendingCleanups[cl.PromotionSeq] = &cl
	f.st.CleanupAudits = append(f.st.CleanupAudits, CleanupAudit{Cleanup: cl, AuthorityJWS: c.AuthorityJWS, AuthorityEpoch: f.st.ConsensusEpoch})
	delete(f.st.LegacyCleanupProofs, cl.PromotionSeq)
	f.emit(Event{Kind: EventCleanupScheduled, PromotionSeq: cl.PromotionSeq})
	return Applied{}
}
```

```go
	if err != nil {

	}

// rejectedCleanupHarness is a leader loop over a published genesis, the
// signed-claims activation (indexer 1: s1; indexer 2: s2; both Active and
// connected), the tracks activation, and db.t's block rejected and released:
// indexer 1's rejected part partHash in db.t/p0 awaits its cleanup. It
// returns the FSM, the node, the SNode directory, the loop, the network
// authority, the block and partHash.
func rejectedCleanupHarness(t *testing.T) (*fsm.FSM, *fakeNode, *fakeSNodes, *Loop, *authority.Signer, uint64, string) {
	t.Helper()
	params, signer := authorityParamsO(t)
	f, node, _, fsn, _, o, _ := newHarness(t, params, signer)
	seedGenesisWriterAndVerifiers(t, node)
	enableRegistryViaNode(t, node, f, params, signer)
	activateSignedClaimsO(t, node, f, signer)
	registerSignedSNodeO(t, node, f, authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex1), "s2", 1)
	applyTracksUpdateO(t, node, f, signer, nil)
	if !f.TracksActive() {
		t.Fatal("tracks not active")
	}
	setSNodeConnections(fsn, []string{"s1", "s2"})
	partHash := lthashHexO("rowA")
	block := rejectedBlockO(t, node, f, partHash)
	releaseO(t, node, f, signer, 1, 1, block)
	return f, node, fsn, o, signer, block, partHash
}

// sentCleanup is one rejected-part cleanup fsn received.
type sentCleanup struct {
	to      string
	cleanup arbiter.UnsafeCleanup
	jws     string
}

// rejectedCleanupsSent lists, in send order, the rejected-part cleanups fsn
// received.
func rejectedCleanupsSent(fsn *fakeSNodes) []sentCleanup {
	fsn.mu.Lock()
	defer fsn.mu.Unlock()
	var out []sentCleanup
	for i, pc := range fsn.sent {
		if c := pc.GetCleanup(); c != nil && c.GetRejectedBlockSeq() != 0 {
			out = append(out, sentCleanup{to: fsn.to[i], cleanup: wire.CleanupFromPB(c), jws: pc.GetAuthorityJws()})
		}
	}
	return out
}

// TestRejectedCleanupIsScheduledAndStreamedToTheBlockSource (contract §3.6):
// the leader schedules a released block's rejected parts through
// ScheduleUnsafeCleanup, signed like any cleanup, and streams the cleanup,
// scheduled or resent, only to the shared source of the block's Rejected
// statements, on every pass until that source acknowledges it.
func TestRejectedCleanupIsScheduledAndStreamedToTheBlockSource(t *testing.T) {
	f, node, fsn, o, signer, block, partHash := rejectedCleanupHarness(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	want := arbiter.UnsafeCleanup{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p0", RejectedBlockSeq: block,
		Parts: []arbiter.PartRef{{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p0", PartRowLtHash: partHash, PartName: "all_1_0"}}}
	ws, err := f.WorkSet()
	if err != nil || len(ws.RejectedUncleaned) != 1 || len(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups) != 0 || !reflect.DeepEqual(ws.RejectedUncleaned[0].Cleanup, want) {
		t.Fatalf("rejected-part work after the release: %+v / %+v, %v", ws.RejectedUncleaned, ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups, err)
	}
	if err := o.handlePromotionRows(ctx, fsm.WorkSet{RejectedUncleaned: ws.RejectedUncleaned}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ws, err = f.WorkSet()
	if err != nil || len(ws.RejectedUncleaned) != 0 || len(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("after the first pass: %d unscheduled, %d scheduled rejected-part cleanups (%v), want 0 and 1",
			len(ws.RejectedUncleaned), len(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups), err)
	}
	validator := authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: map[string]bool{signer.Address(): true}, MaxTokenAge: time.Minute}
	sent := rejectedCleanupsSent(fsn)
	if len(sent) != 1 || sent[0].to != "s1" || !reflect.DeepEqual(sent[0].cleanup, want) {
		t.Fatalf("sent %+v, want the cleanup addressed to s1 alone", sent)
	}
	if _, err := validator.AuthorizeCleanup(sent[0].cleanup, sent[0].jws); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the scheduled cleanup's token: %v", err)
	}
	for pass := 0; pass < 2; pass++ {
		if err := o.handlePromotionRows(ctx, fsm.WorkSet{ScheduledRejectedCleanups: ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	sent = rejectedCleanupsSent(fsn)
	if len(sent) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("sent %d rejected-part cleanups after two resend passes, want 3", len(sent))
	}
	for _, s := range sent {
		if s.to != "s1" {
			t.Fatalf("a rejected-part cleanup went to %s, want only s1", s.to)
		}
		if _, err := validator.AuthorizeCleanup(s.cleanup, s.jws); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("a resent cleanup's token: %v", err)
		}
	}
	ack := wire.CleanupAckFromPB(wire.CleanupAckToPB(arbiter.CleanupAck{NodeID: "s1", TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p0", RejectedBlockSeq: block}))
	jws, err := authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex0).SignSNodeMessage(authority.SNodeMessageCleanupAck, messageContextO(t, f), ack)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	mustApplyViaNode(t, node, wire.Command{RecordCleanupAck: &wire.RecordCleanupAck{Ack: ack, SourceJWS: jws}})
	if ws, err := f.WorkSet(); err != nil || ws.RejectedUncleaned != nil || ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rejected-part work after the source's acknowledgement: %+v / %+v, %v", ws.RejectedUncleaned, ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups, err)
	}
}

// TestScheduledRejectedCleanupIsResignedUnderTheCurrentAuthority (contract
// §3.6, spec §7.4): a scheduled rejected-part cleanup survives a quarantine
// and an authority rotation; after the release the resend path re-signs it
// under the new authority and epoch, and the rotated-out signer sends nothing.
func TestScheduledRejectedCleanupIsResignedUnderTheCurrentAuthority(t *testing.T) {
	f, node, fsn, o, signerA, block, _ := rejectedCleanupHarness(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	ws, err := f.WorkSet()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := o.handlePromotionRows(ctx, fsm.WorkSet{RejectedUncleaned: ws.RejectedUncleaned}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	quarantineO(t, node, f, signerA, 1, 2, "rejected block under review")
	if ws, err := f.WorkSet(); err != nil || len(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a quarantined track's scheduled cleanup stayed in the WorkSet: %+v, %v", ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups, err)
	}
	_, signerB := authorityParamsO(t)
	applyTracksUpdateO(t, node, f, signerA, func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) { u.AuthorityAddresses = []string{signerB.Address()} })
	releaseO(t, node, f, signerB, 1, 3)
	ws, err = f.WorkSet()
	if err != nil || len(ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups) != 1 || ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups[0].Cleanup.RejectedBlockSeq != block {
		t.Fatalf("the released track's scheduled cleanup: %+v, %v", ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups, err)
	}
	before := len(rejectedCleanupsSent(fsn))
	if err := o.handlePromotionRows(ctx, fsm.WorkSet{ScheduledRejectedCleanups: ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := len(rejectedCleanupsSent(fsn)); got != before {
		t.Fatalf("the rotated-out signer sent %d cleanups", got-before)
	}
	deps := o.d
	deps.Signer = signerB
	current := New(deps)
	if err := current.handlePromotionRows(ctx, fsm.WorkSet{ScheduledRejectedCleanups: ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sent := rejectedCleanupsSent(fsn)
	if len(sent) != before+1 || sent[len(sent)-1].to != "s1" {
		t.Fatalf("sent %+v, want one more cleanup addressed to s1", sent)
	}
	last := sent[len(sent)-1]
	validatorB := authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: map[string]bool{signerB.Address(): true}, MaxTokenAge: time.Minute}
	if _, err := validatorB.AuthorizeCleanup(last.cleanup, last.jws); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the resent cleanup does not authorize under the new authority: %v", err)
	}
	validatorA := authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: map[string]bool{signerA.Address(): true}, MaxTokenAge: time.Minute}
	if _, err := validatorA.AuthorizeCleanup(last.cleanup, last.jws); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("the resent cleanup still authorizes under the rotated-out authority")
	}
	payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(strings.Split(last.jws, ".")[1])
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var claims authority.JWSCommandPayload
	if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &claims); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if epoch := authorityContextO(t, f).AuthorityEpoch; claims.AuthorityEpoch == nil || *claims.AuthorityEpoch != epoch {
		t.Fatalf("resent token epoch = %v, want the current epoch %d", claims.AuthorityEpoch, epoch)
	}
}
```

```go
func (o *Loop) streamCleanupSigned(ctx context.Context, cmd arbiter.UnsafeCleanup, jws string) error {
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := o.d.Node.VerifyLeader(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("verify leader before cleanup send: %w", err)
	}
	if !o.authoritySignerReady("cleanup send") {
		return nil
	}
	msg := wire.CleanupCommandPB(cmd, jws)
	for _, id := range o.cleanupTargets(cmd) {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if !o.authoritySignerReady("cleanup send") {
			return nil
		}
		if err := o.d.SNodes.Send(id, msg); err != nil {
			o.d.Logger.Warn("cleanup send failed", "snode", id, "promotion_seq", cmd.PromotionSeq, "rejected_block_seq", cmd.RejectedBlockSeq, "err", err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// cleanupTargets lists the SNodes a cleanup is sent to. A rejected-part
// cleanup (contract §3.6) goes to the shared source of its block's Rejected
// statements, the only node whose acknowledgement the FSM takes, whether or
// not it is connected (a failed send is retried on the next pass); every
// other cleanup follows its promotion (promotionTargets), as before. When
// the FSM cannot name the source nothing is sent.
func (o *Loop) cleanupTargets(cmd arbiter.UnsafeCleanup) []string {
	if cmd.RejectedBlockSeq == 0 {
		return o.promotionTargets(cmd.PromotionSeq)
	}
	node, err := o.d.FSM.RejectedCleanupSource(cmd.RejectedBlockSeq)
	if err != nil {
		o.d.Logger.Warn("rejected-part cleanup not sent: no expected source", "rejected_block_seq", cmd.RejectedBlockSeq, "err", err)
		return nil
	}
	return []string{node}
}
```

Notes:
- **Bytes before the activation.** Every v20 member is `omitempty` (`Params.tracks_enabled`, `tracks`, a header's `track`, the open block's `owner`) and nothing writes one before the activation, so the writer keeps v14–v19 byte for byte. Task 6's frozen pre-tracks golden (which pins `snapshot_version` 19 for a pre-activation multi-owner history), `TestPreActivationHistoryIsByteIdenticalAcrossSignedClaims` (v18), `TestSnapshotStaysPreV19UntilActivation`, `TestSnapshotV19AfterActivationRoundTrips` and the new `TestSnapshotStaysPreV20UntilActivation` pass unchanged.
- **Older-binary refusal.** arbiter `v0.11.0`'s acceptance chain ends at 19 (`fsm/snapshot.go:259` at `e896c41`), so it refuses a v20 container before parsing it (`unsupported snapshot version 20`). `TestSnapshotRefusesTheNextVersion` pins the mechanism one version up; Task 15's release step should run the real `v0.11.0` binary against a real v20 container, as S1 Task 12 Step 5 did for v19.
- **Before Task 12** a tracks-active state is written as v19 without its `tracks` member, so it cannot be restored; no task before this one restores one. After it a tracks-active state always writes v20.
- **Order inside `readSnapshot`.** The v20 block runs after the signed-claims block and before `validateRestoredState`, like the v19 block: a forged member names the version, a corrupt track state names its rule, never a downstream symptom. `validateTrackState` visits indexers, blocks and rejected partitions in sorted order, so every replica names the same corruption.
- **Restore of what Task 9 publishes (G4-1, G4-2).** A configured restore re-checks every manifest against the table-set history with a running union and requires each to advance its parent; after the activation a manifest may carry its parent's label (C6) and two tracks' transitions pinned to one base never form a union (C1), so track-aware manifests take `validateRestoredTrackManifest`. Every restore (bare too) judges each incarnation's status against the global watermark; per-track flips are judged against the incarnation's own track's published frontier (`incarnationPublishedSeq`). Pre-activation states take exactly today's paths.
- **validateTrackState** implements contract §3.7's rules with the checks G4-5 adds: an entry's initial frontier names its own indexer, the cutover lies within the sealed chain and the promotion sequence, rejected partitions are strictly ordered, and before the activation no header has a track and the open block no owner (also under a v20 byte).

```go
// tmV20Fixture fills every v20 member: newTrackManifestFixture; indexer 1's
// block 2 published (a track-aware manifest); indexer 2's block 3 (db2.x: two
// parts in p0, one in p1) rejected by a challenge, which quarantines indexer 2
// automatically, released acknowledging block 3, which records its rejected
// parts, and quarantined again by the authority; and one statement of indexer
// 1 left in the open block. It returns the fixture, the rejected block and its
// statement.
func tmV20Fixture(t *testing.T) (*tmFixture, uint64, uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	x := newTrackManifestFixture(t)
	a := x.write("db.t", tmPart{"p0", "v20-a"})
	b2 := x.seal()
	x.settle(b2)
	x.ack(x.promote(a, "p0"))
	x.publish()
	r := x.write("db2.x", tmPart{"p0", "v20-r1"}, tmPart{"p0", "v20-r2"}, tmPart{"p1", "v20-r3"})
	b3 := x.seal()
	x.reject(b3)
	x.release(2, b3)
	x.quarantine(2, "maintenance")
	x.write("db.t", tmPart{"p1", "v20-open"})
	it, tracks := x.f.indexerTrackLocked(2), x.f.st.Tracks
	if it == nil || !it.Quarantined || it.QuarantineGeneration != 3 || len(it.Rejected) != 0 || len(it.Acknowledged) != 1 || it.Acknowledged[0] != b3 ||
		len(tracks.RejectedParts) != 2 || len(tracks.RejectedParts[0].Parts) != 2 || x.f.st.OpenBlock.Owner == nil || *x.f.st.OpenBlock.Owner != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("v20 fixture: indexer 2 %+v, rejected parts %+v, open block %+v", it, tracks.RejectedParts, x.f.st.OpenBlock)
	}
	return x, b3, r
}

// TestSnapshotStaysPreV20UntilActivation: until tracks_enabled is committed
// the writer keeps v14..v19 byte for byte, with none of the new members, and
// each of those containers restores to the identical bytes.
func TestSnapshotStaysPreV20UntilActivation(t *testing.T) {
	lanes, _, _ := lanesFSM(t, 256)
	claims, _ := ownerFSMWithAuthority(t)
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		f    *FSM
		want byte
	}{
		"registry disabled": {newTestFSM(t), snapshotVersionV14},
		"registry seeded":   {seededRegistryFSM(t), snapshotVersionV15},
		"lanes active":      {lanes, snapshotVersionV18},
		"signed claims":     {claims, snapshotVersionV19},
	} {
		b := snapshotBytes(t, tc.f)
		if b[4] != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("%s: version byte = %d, want %d", name, b[4], tc.want)
		}
		for _, key := range tracksSnapshotKeys {
			if bytes.Contains(b, []byte(key)) {
				t.Fatalf("%s: a pre-activation container carries %s", name, key)
			}
		}
		if got := snapshotBytes(t, restoreInto(t, b)); !bytes.Equal(got, b) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: restore ∘ snapshot is not the identity", name)
		}
	}
}

// TestSnapshotV20AfterActivationRoundTrips: the activation alone selects
// v20; a container holding every v20 member — the cutover and initial
// entries, a track-aware manifest, header tracks, a rejected, acknowledged
// and again quarantined track with rejected parts awaiting cleanup, and an
// owned open block — restores (bare and through the configured production
// path) and re-encodes identically; the capacity counter mirrors it.
func TestSnapshotV20AfterActivationRoundTrips(t *testing.T) {
	if b := snapshotBytes(t, newTrackManifestFixture(t).f); b[4] != snapshotVersionV20 || !bytes.Contains(b, []byte(`"tracks":`)) {
		t.Fatalf("right after the activation: version byte %d", b[4])
	}
	x, rejected, _ := tmV20Fixture(t)
	b := snapshotBytes(t, x.f)
	if b[4] != snapshotVersionV20 {
		t.Fatalf("version byte = %d, want 20", b[4])
	}
	restored := restoreInto(t, b)
	got, err := json.Marshal(restored.st.Tracks)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want, err := json.Marshal(x.f.st.Tracks)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !restored.TracksActive() || !bytes.Equal(got, want) || restored.st.OpenBlock.Owner == nil || *restored.st.OpenBlock.Owner != 1 ||
		restored.st.Blocks[rejected-1].Track == nil || restored.st.Blocks[rejected-1].Track.IndexerID != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("restored tracks %s, open block %+v, block %d %+v", got, restored.st.OpenBlock, rejected, restored.st.Blocks[rejected-1])
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(snapshotBytes(t, restored), b) {
		t.Fatal("restore ∘ snapshot is not the identity")
	}
	if _, err := restoreConfigured(t, x.f, b); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("configured restore: %v", err)
	}
	dims, err := CountSnapshotEncoding(x.f.st)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if n := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[5:13]); dims.JSONBytes != n {
		t.Fatalf("counted %d document bytes, container holds %d", dims.JSONBytes, n)
	}
}

// TestPreV20ContainerCarryingTracksIsRefused: any v20 member under an older
// version byte is a forged field, not a migration, each one alone and even
// when empty.
func TestPreV20ContainerCarryingTracksIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	forged := rewriteSnapshotDocument(t, snapshotBytes(t, newTrackManifestFixture(t).f), snapshotVersionV19, keepSnapshotDocument)
	if err := restoreErr(t, forged); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "pre-v20") {
		t.Fatalf("v20 relabelled v19: %v", err)
	}
	plain := snapshotBytes(t, publishedTransitionFSM(t))
	if plain[4] != snapshotVersionV16 {
		t.Fatalf("fixture version byte = %d, want 16", plain[4])
	}
	for name, mutate := range map[string]func(map[string]any){
		"params tracks_enabled":    func(doc map[string]any) { v20Params(doc)["tracks_enabled"] = true },
		"bootstrap tracks_enabled": func(doc map[string]any) { doc["bootstrap_params"].(map[string]any)["tracks_enabled"] = true },
		"empty tracks":             func(doc map[string]any) { doc["tracks"] = map[string]any{} },
		"header track":             func(doc map[string]any) { v20Block(doc, 1)["track"] = map[string]any{"indexer_id": 0} },
		"open block owner":         func(doc map[string]any) { v20OpenBlock(doc)["owner"] = 0 },
	} {
		for _, version := range []byte{snapshotVersionV16, snapshotVersionV17, snapshotVersionV18, snapshotVersionV19} {
			forged := rewriteSnapshotDocument(t, plain, version, mutate)
			if _, err := readSnapshot(bytes.NewReader(forged)); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "pre-v20") {
				t.Fatalf("%s under v%d: readSnapshot = %v, want a pre-v20 refusal", name, version, err)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestSnapshotVersionChainsCoverV19AndV20: every version chain in
// readSnapshot names v19 and v20 now that snapshotVersion moved on.
func TestSnapshotVersionChainsCoverV19AndV20(t *testing.T) {
	claims, _ := ownerFSMWithAuthority(t)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		version byte
		data    []byte
	}{
		{snapshotVersionV19, snapshotBytes(t, claims)},
		{snapshotVersionV20, snapshotBytes(t, newTrackManifestFixture(t).f)},
	} {
		forged := rewriteSnapshotDocument(t, tc.data, tc.version, func(doc map[string]any) { delete(doc, "bootstrap_params") })
		if _, err := readSnapshot(bytes.NewReader(forged)); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "missing bootstrap consensus params") {
			t.Fatalf("v%d without bootstrap_params: readSnapshot = %v", tc.version, err)
		}
	}
}

	if err := restoreErr(t, next); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unsupported snapshot version 21") {

}
```

```go
// snapshotVersion is the newest container this binary writes. writeSnapshot
// writes it only once Params.TracksEnabled is committed (the tracks
// activation, housegate spec 2026-10-10 §7.6); before that it writes
// snapshotVersionV19 once Params.SIIndexers is committed (the signed-claims
// activation, §6.7), snapshotVersionV18 once Params.ClientLanes is committed
// (client_seq lanes, housegate spec 2026-10-09 §5.4), snapshotVersionV17 once
// an incarnation carries a refused_code or retire_reason (sub-project 2c),
// snapshotVersionV16 once a sealed block carries a table-set transition,
// snapshotVersionV15 while the SI table registry is enabled, and
// snapshotVersionV14 while both Params.TableRegistry and State.TableRegistry
// are nil. Each step keeps rollback and snapshot installs on not-yet-upgraded
// followers working until the state actually needs the newer container. An
// older binary must never load a field it would drop on its next snapshot (a
// transition header, whose loss would change the chain hash, the v17 registry
// fields, v18's client_lanes and lane_counts, v19's si_indexers, verifiers,
// registration_seqs, incarnation owners and seeded indexers, or v20's
// tracks_enabled, tracks state, header tracks and open-block owner, whose loss
// would change chain hashes or make replicas' states differ), so each version
// byte is what makes the older binary refuse.
const (
	snapshotVersion       = 20
	snapshotVersionV20    = 20
	snapshotVersionV19    = 19
	snapshotVersionV18    = 18
	snapshotVersionV17    = 17
	snapshotVersionV16    = 16
	snapshotVersionV15    = 15
	snapshotVersionV14    = 14
	snapshotVersionV13    = 13
	snapshotVersionV12    = 12
	snapshotVersionV11    = 11
	snapshotVersionV10    = 10
	snapshotVersionV9     = 9
	snapshotVersionV8     = 8
	snapshotVersionV7     = 7
	snapshotVersionV6     = 6
	snapshotVersionV5     = 5
	snapshotVersionV4     = 4
	legacySnapshotVersion = 3
	maxSnapshotDocBytes   = 1 << 30
)
```

`snapshotWriteVersion` (181-205):

```go
// snapshotWriteVersion is snapshotVersion (v20) once tracks_enabled is
// committed, snapshotVersionV19 once si_indexers is committed,
// snapshotVersionV18 once client lanes are committed, snapshotVersionV17 once
// any incarnation carries a v17 field, snapshotVersionV16 once any sealed
// block carries a table-set transition, snapshotVersionV15 while the table
// registry is enabled without either, and snapshotVersionV14 while it is
// disabled; see snapshotVersion.
func snapshotWriteVersion(st *State) byte {
	if st.Params.TracksEnabled {
		return snapshotVersionV20
	}
	if len(st.Params.SIIndexers) > 0 {
		return snapshotVersionV19
	}
	if st.Params.ClientLanes != nil {
		return snapshotVersionV18
	}
	if tableRegistryHasV17Fields(st.TableRegistry) {
		return snapshotVersionV17
	}
	for _, header := range st.Blocks {
		if header.TableSetTransition != nil {
			return snapshotVersionV16
		}
	}
	if st.TableRegistry == nil && st.Params.TableRegistry == nil {
		return snapshotVersionV14
	}
	return snapshotVersionV15
}
```

```go
// tracksFieldsPresent reports any member only a v20 container may hold.
func tracksFieldsPresent(doc *snapshotDoc) bool {
	if doc.Params.TracksEnabled || doc.Tracks != nil {
		return true
	}
	if b := doc.BootstrapParams; b != nil && b.TracksEnabled {
		return true
	}
	if doc.OpenBlock != nil && doc.OpenBlock.Owner != nil {
		return true
	}
	for _, header := range doc.Blocks {
		if header.Track != nil {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

```go
package fsm

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
)

// validateTrackState checks the stage-2 state a restored container carries
// (spec 2026-10-10 §7.4-§7.6, contract §3.7, with the checks of proposed
// amendment G4-5). Before the tracks activation no track state exists: no
// tracks member, no header track, no open-block owner. After it the state is
// exactly what Apply produces: one track per si_indexers entry, ascending,
// each with its own initial frontier at or after a cutover that lies within
// the chain; no track on a block at or below the cutover and an enrolled one
// on every later block; transition blocks changing only their own track's
// tables; an open block owned exactly when it holds statements; rejected and
// acknowledged blocks ascending, disjoint and naming Rejected blocks of their
// track; a reason on every quarantine; and rejected-part cleanup work strictly
// ordered, naming acknowledged blocks and non-empty sorted part lists.
// Indexers, blocks and rejected partitions are visited in sorted order so
// every replica names the same corruption.
func validateTrackState(st *State) error {
	tracks, ob := st.Tracks, st.OpenBlock
	if st.Params.TracksEnabled != (tracks != nil) {
		return fmt.Errorf("tracks state must exist exactly when tracks_enabled is committed")
	}
	if tracks == nil {
		for _, h := range st.Blocks {
			if h.Track != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("block %d carries a track before the tracks activation", h.L3BlockSeq)
			}
		}
		if ob != nil && ob.Owner != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("the open block has an owner before the tracks activation")
		}
		return nil
	}
	view := &FSM{st: st}
	if len(tracks.Indexers) != len(st.Params.SIIndexers) {
		return fmt.Errorf("tracks must hold one entry per si_indexers entry: %d entries for %d indexers", len(tracks.Indexers), len(st.Params.SIIndexers))
	}
	for i, it := range tracks.Indexers {
		if i > 0 && it.IndexerID <= tracks.Indexers[i-1].IndexerID {
			return fmt.Errorf("tracks indexers must be sorted by indexer id and unique")
		}
		if _, ok := findSIIndexer(st.Params.SIIndexers, it.IndexerID); !ok {
			return fmt.Errorf("tracks names indexer %d, which has no si_indexers entry", it.IndexerID)
		}
		if it.Initial.IndexerID != it.IndexerID {
			return fmt.Errorf("tracks entry of indexer %d carries the initial frontier of indexer %d", it.IndexerID, it.Initial.IndexerID)
		}
	}
	cutover := tracks.Cutover
	if cutover.BlockSeq > uint64(len(st.Blocks)) || cutover.PromotionSeq > st.PromotionSeq {
		return fmt.Errorf("tracks cutover {%d %d} lies beyond the sealed chain or the promotion sequence", cutover.BlockSeq, cutover.PromotionSeq)
	}
	for _, it := range tracks.Indexers {
		if it.Initial.SafeBlockSeq < cutover.BlockSeq || it.Initial.AppliedPromotionSeq < cutover.PromotionSeq {
			return fmt.Errorf("initial frontier of indexer %d is below the tracks cutover {%d %d}", it.IndexerID, cutover.BlockSeq, cutover.PromotionSeq)
		}
	}
	for idx, h := range st.Blocks {
		seq := uint64(idx + 1)
		if seq <= cutover.BlockSeq {
			if h.Track != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("block %d at or below the tracks cutover carries a track", seq)
			}
			continue
		}
		if h.Track == nil || view.indexerTrackLocked(h.Track.IndexerID) == nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("block %d after the tracks cutover names no enrolled indexer", seq)
		}
		if h.TableSetTransition != nil {
			if err := view.validateTransitionTrackLocked(seq, h); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	if ob != nil {
		if (len(ob.StatementSeqs) != 0) != (ob.Owner != nil) {
			return fmt.Errorf("the open block has an owner exactly when it holds statements")
		}
		if ob.Owner != nil && view.indexerTrackLocked(*ob.Owner) == nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("the open block names indexer %d, which is not enrolled", *ob.Owner)
		}
	}
	acknowledged := map[uint64]bool{}
	for _, it := range tracks.Indexers {
		if err := view.validateRejectedBlocksLocked(it.IndexerID, "rejected", it.Rejected); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := view.validateRejectedBlocksLocked(it.IndexerID, "acknowledged", it.Acknowledged); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		for _, b := range it.Rejected {
			if slices.Contains(it.Acknowledged, b) {
				return fmt.Errorf("indexer %d lists block %d as both rejected and acknowledged", it.IndexerID, b)
			}
		}
		if it.Quarantined && it.QuarantineReason == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("quarantined indexer %d has no quarantine reason", it.IndexerID)
		}
		for _, b := range it.Acknowledged {
			acknowledged[b] = true
		}
	}
	for i, rp := range tracks.RejectedParts {
		if i > 0 && !restoredRejectedPartitionBefore(tracks.RejectedParts[i-1], rp) {
			return fmt.Errorf("rejected parts must be sorted by block, table and partition and unique")
		}
		if !acknowledged[rp.BlockSeq] {
			return fmt.Errorf("rejected partition of block %d names no acknowledged block of a track", rp.BlockSeq)
		}
		if len(rp.Parts) == 0 || !restoredPartRefsSorted(rp.Parts) {
			return fmt.Errorf("rejected partition of block %d table %s partition %s has no parts or unsorted parts", rp.BlockSeq, rp.TableID, rp.PartitionID)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// validateTransitionTrackLocked checks that transition block seq changes only
// tables its track owns. An add or retire without a matching incarnation is
// validateTableSetTransitions' refusal, not this one's, and so is a
// transition without a registry.
func (f *FSM) validateTransitionTrackLocked(seq uint64, h L3BlockHeader) error {
	reg := f.st.TableRegistry
	if reg == nil || f.st.Params.TableRegistry == nil {
		return nil
	}
	track := h.Track.IndexerID
	check := func(tableID string, changedBy func(*TableIncarnation) bool) error {
		for _, inc := range reg.Incarnations {
			if inc == nil || inc.Key() != tableID || !changedBy(inc) {
				continue
			}
			if owner := f.incarnationOwnerLocked(inc); owner != track {
				return fmt.Errorf("table-set transition block %d changes %s of indexer %d, not of its track %d", seq, tableID, owner, track)
			}
			return nil
		}
		return nil
	}
	for _, add := range h.TableSetTransition.Adds {
		if err := check(add.TableID, func(inc *TableIncarnation) bool { return inc.AddBlockSeq == seq }); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	for _, tableID := range h.TableSetTransition.Retires {
		if err := check(tableID, func(inc *TableIncarnation) bool { return inc.RetireBlockSeq == seq }); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// validateRejectedBlocksLocked checks one of track id's rejected-block lists
// (name is "rejected" or "acknowledged"): strictly ascending, and every entry
// a block of that track holding a Rejected statement.
func (f *FSM) validateRejectedBlocksLocked(id uint64, name string, blocks []uint64) error {
	for i, b := range blocks {
		if i > 0 && b <= blocks[i-1] {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s blocks of indexer %d must be ascending and unique", name, id)
		}
		rejected := func(ss *StatementState) bool { return ss.Status == StatusRejected }
		if b == 0 || b > uint64(len(f.st.Blocks)) || f.st.Blocks[b-1].Track == nil || f.st.Blocks[b-1].Track.IndexerID != id ||
			!slices.ContainsFunc(f.blockStatements(b), rejected) {
			return fmt.Errorf("indexer %d lists %s block %d, which is not a block of its track holding a Rejected statement", id, name, b)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// restoredRejectedPartitionBefore orders rejected partitions by block, table
// and partition, the order TrackState.RejectedParts keeps.
func restoredRejectedPartitionBefore(a, b RejectedPartition) bool {
	if a.BlockSeq != b.BlockSeq {
		return a.BlockSeq < b.BlockSeq
	}
	if a.TableID != b.TableID {
		return a.TableID < b.TableID
	}
	return a.PartitionID < b.PartitionID
}

// restoredPartRefsSorted reports whether parts are strictly ascending by row
// hash, the order a release records them in (contract §3.6).
func restoredPartRefsSorted(parts []arbiter.PartRef) bool {
	for i := 1; i < len(parts); i++ {
		if parts[i].PartRowLtHash <= parts[i-1].PartRowLtHash {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}
```

```go
package fsm

// TestSnapshotV20RestoresPerTrackPublications (per proposed amendments G4-1
// and G4-2): in the container indexer 2's transition is published while
// indexer 1's, pinned to the same base, is not, so db2.w is Active above the
// global watermark and m1 carries its parent's safe_block_seq. It restores
// bare and through the configured path; a missing or premature per-track flip
// is refused, and so are a frontier-less manifest above the cutover and a
// track-aware manifest whose tables are not its frontiers' table set.
func TestSnapshotV20RestoresPerTrackPublications(t *testing.T) {
	s := tmPinnedTransitions(t)
	f := s.x.f
	data := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	if data[4] != snapshotVersionV20 || s.m1.SafeBlockSeq != s.m0.SafeBlockSeq || f.st.TableRegistry.Live("db2.w").AddBlockSeq <= f.st.SafeWatermark.SafeBlockSeq {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: version %d, m1 labelled %d over m0's %d", data[4], s.m1.SafeBlockSeq, s.m0.SafeBlockSeq)
	}
	g := restoreInto(t, data)
	if !bytes.Equal(snapshotBytes(t, g), data) {
		t.Fatal("restore ∘ snapshot is not the identity")
	}
	restoreCheckpoint(t, f, "per-track publication", func(t *testing.T, r *FSM) {
		if w, y := r.st.TableRegistry.Live("db2.w").Status, r.st.TableRegistry.Live("db.y").Status; w != TableStatusActive || y != TableStatusPending {
			t.Fatalf("restored statuses db2.w %s, db.y %s", w, y)
		}
		if m := r.st.Manifests[r.st.SafeWatermark.SnapshotID]; m == nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(m.TrackFrontiers, s.m1.TrackFrontiers) {
			t.Fatalf("restored watermark manifest = %+v", m)
		}
	})
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct{ table, status string }{
		"premature flip": {"y", "active"},
		"missing flip":   {"w", "pending"},
	} {
		forged := rewriteSnapshotDocument(t, data, snapshotVersionV20, func(doc map[string]any) { liveIncarnation(doc, tc.table)["status"] = tc.status })
		if err := restoreErr(t, forged); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "disagrees with its transition blocks") {
			t.Fatalf("%s: restore = %v", name, err)
		}
	}
	genesis := g.st.Manifests[mustGenesisID(t, g)]
	m1 := g.st.Manifests[s.m1.SnapshotID]
	plain := tmReseal(t, *m1, func(m *replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) { m.TrackFrontiers, m.SafeBlockSeq = nil, s.blockW })
	g.st.Manifests[plain.SnapshotID] = &plain
	if err := validateRestoredManifests(g.st, genesis); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "carries no track_frontiers after the tracks activation") {
		t.Fatalf("frontier-less manifest above the cutover: %v", err)
	}
	delete(g.st.Manifests, plain.SnapshotID)
	extra := tmReseal(t, *m1, func(m *replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) {
		m.Tables = append(m.Tables, replay.TableManifest{TableID: "db.zz", SchemaHash: m.Tables[0].SchemaHash})
		m.SchemaRoot = payloadexec.SchemaRootFromHashes(manifestSchemaSet(m))
	})
	g.st.Manifests[extra.SnapshotID] = &extra
	if err := validateRestoredManifests(g.st, genesis); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "has a different genesis identity") {
		t.Fatalf("track-aware manifest with a foreign table: %v", err)
	}
	delete(g.st.Manifests, extra.SnapshotID)
	if err := validateRestoredManifests(g.st, genesis); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("restored manifests: %v", err)
	}
}
```

```go
// headers and registry disagree. A transition header is replicated content
```

```go
// incarnationPublishedSeq is the block up to which inc's transition blocks are
// published: the global safe watermark before the tracks activation; after
// it, the published frontier of the track of inc's owner — the latest
// manifest's entry for it, else its initial entry — since Pending→Active and
// Retiring→Purging advance per track (contract §3.4). A transition block
// sealed before the activation lies at or below the cutover, which every
// published frontier reaches, so its incarnations are judged alike under
// either rule.
func incarnationPublishedSeq(st *State, inc *TableIncarnation) uint64 {
	if st.Tracks == nil {
		return st.SafeWatermark.SafeBlockSeq
	}
	view := &FSM{st: st}
	return view.publishedTrackFrontierLocked(view.incarnationOwnerLocked(inc)).SafeBlockSeq
}
```

After `validateRestoredManifestsWalk`:

```go
// validateRestoredTrackManifest checks one track-aware manifest of a restored
// container against the configured genesis (clarification C1): it exists only
// after the tracks activation and every manifest labelled above the cutover
// is one; no entry names a block beyond the sealed chain; its table set is
// genesis with every transition block it covers applied in block order through
// resultSet — a block without a track (sealed before the activation) at or
// below its safe_block_seq, a block of track t at or below t's entry — and its
// schema_root is SchemaRootFromHashes over that set; its part ledger is
// consistent; and its parent exists with a safe_block_seq no higher than its
// own (C6). A transition root is never compared with a running union.
func validateRestoredTrackManifest(st *State, genesis *replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, transitions []uint64, id string, m *replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) error {
	switch {
	case st.Tracks == nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("snapshot manifest %q carries track_frontiers before the tracks activation", id)
	case len(m.TrackFrontiers) == 0:
		return fmt.Errorf("snapshot manifest %q carries no track_frontiers after the tracks activation", id)
	}
	entries := make(map[uint64]uint64, len(m.TrackFrontiers))
	for _, entry := range m.TrackFrontiers {
		if entry.SafeBlockSeq > uint64(len(st.Blocks)) {
			return fmt.Errorf("snapshot manifest %q track_frontiers entry of indexer %d names block %d beyond the sealed chain", id, entry.IndexerID, entry.SafeBlockSeq)
		}
		entries[entry.IndexerID] = entry.SafeBlockSeq
	}
	schemas := manifestSchemaSet(genesis)
	for _, seq := range transitions {
		h := st.Blocks[seq-1]
		covered := false
		if h.Track == nil {
			covered = seq <= m.SafeBlockSeq
		} else if safe, ok := entries[h.Track.IndexerID]; ok {
			covered = seq <= safe
		}
		if !covered {
			continue
		}
		next, err := h.TableSetTransition.resultSet(schemas)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("snapshot manifest %q table set: block %d: %w", id, seq, err)
		}
		schemas = next
	}
	if m.SchemaSnapshotID != genesis.SchemaSnapshotID || m.ExecutorProfileID != genesis.ExecutorProfileID || m.SchemaRoot != payloadexec.SchemaRootFromHashes(schemas) {
		return fmt.Errorf("snapshot manifest %q has a different genesis identity", id)
	}
	if err := validateManifestSchemas(m, schemas); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("snapshot manifest %q: %w", id, err)
	}
	parent := st.Manifests[m.ParentSnapshotID]
	if parent == nil || parent.SafeBlockSeq > m.SafeBlockSeq || m.SafeBlockSeq > uint64(len(st.Blocks)) {
		return fmt.Errorf("snapshot manifest %q has no valid parent or sealed block", id)
	}
	return nil
}
```

Notes:
- **Byte-identical before the activation.** Every new path is gated: the quarantine RPCs and `GetTrackState` on `FSM.TracksActive()` (before it they refuse, or answer the empty view, and propose nothing), the tracks gate and its lock on `update.TracksEnabled && !TracksActive()`, the RegisterNode refusal on `TracksActive()`, the AckCleanup refusal on `rejected_block_seq != 0`, the grouping window on a non-zero window, a node that reports leadership and `TracksActive()`, the seal-loop bound, the event seal times and the per-track publication metrics on `TracksActive()` / `TracksEnabled`, custody's track rule after the global rule, and the track gauges on a non-empty `MetricsSnapshot.Tracks`. `proposeTracked` is split into its two halves without changing what any caller sees. `server.Config.SubmissionGroupingWindow` is zero at every construction site except `cmd/arbiter/services.go`, which plumbs the configured value: `cmd/arbiter-admin/client_lanes_test.go:507`, `cmd/arbiter-admin/signed_claims_test.go:456`, `cmd/arbiter-admin/consensus_integration_test.go:160`, `:164`, `:167`, `integration/cluster_node_test.go:100`, `integration/chpipeline/cluster_test.go:278` and every `server` test stay unchanged, so every existing integration test keeps today's path.
- **Strict decoder.** Raft tags 36/37 and `CleanupAck.rejected_block_seq` must never reach a voter before the activation (contract §0). The RPCs refuse from this leader's applied state (the `EvictNode` precedent: the activation is irreversible and applied implies committed). `AckCleanup` uses `tracksCommitted`, which answers a positive from applied state and takes a read barrier before a negative, like `clientLanesCommitted` (`server/ingress.go:130-138`), so a lagging new leader does not refuse a field it may already propose.
- **The tracks gate copies `signedClaimsGate`** (`server/signed_claims_gate.go:51-90`) and its call site: `UpdateConsensusParams` takes `membershipMu.Lock()` and `consensusReadBarrier` when the update first sets `tracks_enabled`, so a `RegisterNode` (which holds `RLock` through its proposal) is either reflected in the gate's read or ordered after the activation, where the new RegisterNode refusal stops a stage-1 binary. The order is: non-voters, then the FSM's own `TracksActivationRefusal()`, then the feature book; Apply decides the FSM preconditions again.
- **Quarantine and release RPCs** keep `EvictNode`'s order (`server/signed_messages.go:42-78`): updates enabled, the activation, shape, `consensusLeaderCheck` (no log write), the committed authority context, `Authorize*` with `MaxTokenAge` (the only clock read), then the proposal. propose maps exactly `fsm.Rejected` to `InvalidArgument` (`server/server.go:264-268`), so `applyRefusalAsFailedPrecondition` turns precisely the FSM's refusals into `FailedPrecondition` with the FSM reason (contract §3.8); NotLeader keeps its detail.
- **`TableOwner` never writes.** `TableRegistryState.Live` builds `r.live` lazily (`fsm/table_registry.go:174-191`), a write that is unsafe under `f.mu.RLock`; `liveReadOnly` uses the index when it exists and otherwise scans `Incarnations` newest first under the same rule. `TestTableOwnerNeverBuildsTheLiveIndex` runs under `-race`.
- **Grouping window ordering.** hashicorp/raft queues `Apply` calls in the order they hand off their futures (`applyCh` is unbuffered, the leader loop group-commits in arrival order), so the grouper's single goroutine submits each closed window's commands through `submitTracked` in owner order and every handler awaits its own future through `awaitTracked`: the log keeps the grouped order while commits still pipeline (Contract conflicts G6a-1). Owners come from `FSM.TableOwner` at the close; a table with no owner goes last. A canceled handler's command is skipped exactly as `proposeTracked` skips it. `OnLeadershipLost` and `Close` answer every not-yet-submitted command with `notLeaderErr`, the follower's error; a window whose submissions were failed carries a stale generation, so its timer does nothing. A node that does not implement `IsLeader() bool` never groups (every fake in the existing tests).
- **Seal loop.** After the activation each owner seals its own transition block while the admission fence holds, so one pass needs at most one drain plus one seal per enrolled indexer (`transitionSealBound`); before it the pass keeps today's two proposals (Contract conflicts G6a-2). After the activation seal times are also taken from `EventBlockSealed` (G6a-3), so owner-switch seals inside admission are timed; `recordSealTime` already ignores a block it has timed.
- **Publication metrics and custody.** After the activation a publication may leave the global watermark in place (C6); `observePublication` times, for every `track_frontiers` entry that moved, exactly `TrackBlocks(id, old, new)` (G6a-4) and leaves other tracks' seal times pending. `CustodyWork.Safe` keeps the global rule first and adds "the block's own track's published frontier covers it" after the activation; `orchestrator/custody.go:43` is unchanged and reads it.
- **C12.** Re-signed work after an authority rotation is accepted only by an SNode whose static `AuthorityAddresses` already lists the new authority (`arbiter-core:snode/snode.go:135`, `:585-591`); `TestReleasedTrackWorkIsRedispatchedUnderTheNewAuthority` checks the dispatched tokens with exactly that validator (`MaxTokenAge` one minute, allowlist `{A, B}`), and additionally under `{B}` alone and against the new epoch's context.
- **CI red lines.** No new fsm file imports arbiter-proto (the pb conversion lives in `server`) and none reads the clock.
- **Helper names.** The fsm, server and orchestrator test helpers above were checked unused at the base revision; they are distinct from anything contract §3 names, so they cannot collide with Tasks 6–12's fixtures unless those pick the same names (Appendix B, Facts).

```go
package fsm

import (

// readsTracksFSM is twoIndexerFSM's network (founding indexer 1 on the Active
// SNode s1, indexer 2 on s2 with activation block 150, verifiers v1..v3, the
// registry cursor completing block 99) after the tracks activation, nothing
// sealed, with its authority.
func readsTracksFSM(t *testing.T) (*FSM, *authority.Signer) {
	t.Helper()
	f, a := claimsFSM(t)
	activateClaims(t, f, a, siEntry(t, f, indexerSigner2(t), 2, 150, "s2"))
	activateReadsTracks(t, f, a)
	return f, a
}

// activateReadsTracks commits the tracks activation carrying every committed
// list (contract §3.1).
func activateReadsTracks(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer) {
	t.Helper()
	u := claimsUpdate(t, f, slices.Clone(f.st.Params.SIIndexers), slices.Clone(f.st.Params.Verifiers))
	u.TracksEnabled = true
	mustApply(t, f, signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, u))
	if !f.TracksActive() {
		t.Fatal("the tracks activation did not commit")
	}
}

// readsQuarantine is the authority-signed QuarantineIndexer of indexer id at
// generation, under f's current authority context.
func readsQuarantine(t *testing.T, f *FSM, a *authority.Signer, id, generation uint64, reason string) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.QuarantineIndexer{IndexerID: id, ExpectedGeneration: generation, Reason: reason}
	token, err := a.SignQuarantineIndexerWithContext(cmd.Canonical(), authorityContextFor(t, f))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cmd.AuthorityJWS = token
	return wire.Command{QuarantineIndexer: &cmd}
}

// readsIndexer2Table completes block 149, seeds indexer 2 there and adds
// db2.x owned by indexer 2 at blocks 150/151, in TestAddTableOwnerAfterActivation's
// order (the unseeded-indexer guard and the activation-block rule both hold).
func readsIndexer2Table(t *testing.T, f *FSM) {
	t.Helper()
	mustApply(t, f, advanceTo(149))
	mustApply(t, f, seedIndexerCmd(2, 149))
	mustApply(t, f, ownedAddCmd(t, f, "db2", "x", ev(150, "0x150", 0), ev(151, "0x151", 0), 2))
}

// TestTableOwnerFollowsTheLiveIncarnation: contract §3.8. The owner of the
// live incarnation, the founding indexer for an incarnation that names none
// (the genesis table and a Legacy table seeded before the signed-claims
// activation), nothing for an unknown table or a disabled registry.
func TestTableOwnerFollowsTheLiveIncarnation(t *testing.T) {
	if _, ok := newTestFSM(t).TableOwner("db.t"); ok {
		t.Fatal("a disabled registry names an owner")
	}
	f := twoIndexerFSM(t)
	readsIndexer2Table(t, f)
	for table, want := range map[string]uint64{"db.t": 1, "db.old": 1, "db2.x": 2} {
		if got, ok := f.TableOwner(table); !ok || got != want {
			t.Fatalf("TableOwner(%s) = %d, %v; want %d", table, got, ok, want)
		}
	}
	if owner, ok := f.TableOwner("db.missing"); ok {
		t.Fatalf("an unknown table has owner %d", owner)
	}
}

// TestLiveReadOnlyAgreesWithLive: the read-only lookup answers exactly what
// Live answers, with and without the derived index.
func TestLiveReadOnlyAgreesWithLive(t *testing.T) {
	f := twoIndexerFSM(t)
	readsIndexer2Table(t, f)
	reg := f.st.TableRegistry
	for _, key := range []string{"db.t", "db.old", "db2.x", "db.missing"} {
		want := reg.Live(key)
		if got := reg.liveReadOnly(key); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("%s with the index: %+v, Live %+v", key, got, want)
		}
		saved := reg.live
		reg.live = nil
		got := reg.liveReadOnly(key)
		built := reg.live != nil
		reg.live = saved
		if got != want || built {
			t.Fatalf("%s without the index: %+v (index built: %v), Live %+v", key, got, built, want)
		}
	}
}

// TestTableOwnerNeverBuildsTheLiveIndex: the grouping window calls TableOwner
// from concurrent ingress handlers under the read lock; with the derived index
// absent the readers scan and none of them writes it (run with -race).
func TestTableOwnerNeverBuildsTheLiveIndex(t *testing.T) {
	f := twoIndexerFSM(t)
	readsIndexer2Table(t, f)
	f.st.TableRegistry.live = nil
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for range 8 {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for range 200 {
				if owner, ok := f.TableOwner("db2.x"); !ok || owner != 2 {
					t.Errorf("TableOwner(db2.x) = %d, %v", owner, ok)
					return
				}
				if owner, ok := f.TableOwner("db.t"); !ok || owner != 1 {
					t.Errorf("TableOwner(db.t) = %d, %v", owner, ok)
					return
				}
				if _, ok := f.TableOwner("db.missing"); ok {
					t.Error("an unknown table has an owner")
					return
				}
			}
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
	if f.st.TableRegistry.live != nil {
		t.Fatal("TableOwner built the derived index under the read lock")
	}
}

// TestTracksActivationRefusalAnswersAsApplyWould: the leader's preflight reads
// the same refusal the activation's Apply returns, and changes nothing.
func TestTracksActivationRefusalAnswersAsApplyWould(t *testing.T) {
	f, a := claimsFSM(t)
	activateClaims(t, f, a)
	if got := f.TracksActivationRefusal(); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("a drained network refuses the activation: %q", got)
	}
	key, account := testAccount(t)
	if r := submit(t, f, registryEnvelope(t, key, account, 1, "db.t", genesisSchemaHash(t, f))); r.Code != arbiter.AdmissionCodeAccepted {

	}

		u := claimsUpdate(t, f, slices.Clone(f.st.Params.SIIndexers), slices.Clone(f.st.Params.Verifiers))
		u.TracksEnabled = true
		return signedConsensusUpdate(t, a, u)
	}
	const openBlock = "tracks activation requires an empty open block"
	if got := f.TracksActivationRefusal(); got != openBlock {
		t.Fatalf("TracksActivationRefusal = %q, want %q", got, openBlock)
	}
	rejectConsensusUnchanged(t, f, activation(), openBlock)
	mustSeal(t, f)
	const unsafeBlock = "tracks activation requires every sealed block to be safe"
	if got := f.TracksActivationRefusal(); got != unsafeBlock {
		t.Fatalf("TracksActivationRefusal = %q, want %q", got, unsafeBlock)
	}
	rejectConsensusUnchanged(t, f, activation(), unsafeBlock)
}
```

Create `fsm/reads_tracks.go`:

```go
package fsm

import (
	"slices"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
)

// TrackStateView is the replicated tracks state as ConsensusAdmin.GetTrackState
// serves it (pb.TrackStateView; housegate spec 2026-10-10 §7, contract §3.8).
// It is the zero value before the tracks activation.
type TrackStateView struct {
	TracksEnabled bool
	// CutoverBlockSeq and CutoverPromotionSeq are the activation point: the
	// sealed tip and PromotionSeq when the activation applied.
	CutoverBlockSeq     uint64
	CutoverPromotionSeq uint64
	// GlobalSafeBlockSeq is the global safe prefix; PublishedSafeBlockSeq is
	// the published manifest's safe_block_seq.
	GlobalSafeBlockSeq    uint64
	PublishedSafeBlockSeq uint64
	// Indexers has one entry per enrolled SI indexer, sorted by indexer id.
	Indexers []IndexerTrackView
}

// IndexerTrackView is one SI indexer's track (pb.IndexerTrackView).
type IndexerTrackView struct {
	IndexerID uint64
	// Initial is the track's frontier before its first own block.
	Initial              replay.TrackFrontier
	QuarantineGeneration uint64
	Quarantined          bool
	QuarantineReason     string
	// RejectedBlocks are the track's rejected blocks no release has
	// acknowledged yet, AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks those a release did; both
	// ascending.
	RejectedBlocks             []uint64
	AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks []uint64
	// PrefixBlockSeq is the track's safe prefix. Published is its entry in the
	// published manifest, Initial until a track-aware manifest names it.
	PrefixBlockSeq uint64
	Published      replay.TrackFrontier
}

// TrackStateView reads the tracks state under the read lock.
func (f *FSM) TrackStateView() TrackStateView {
	f.mu.RLock()
	defer f.mu.RUnlock()
	ts := f.st.Tracks
	if !f.tracksActiveLocked() || ts == nil {
		return TrackStateView{}
	}
	v := TrackStateView{
		TracksEnabled:         true,
		CutoverBlockSeq:       ts.Cutover.BlockSeq,
		CutoverPromotionSeq:   ts.Cutover.PromotionSeq,
		GlobalSafeBlockSeq:    safePrefixLocked(f),
		PublishedSafeBlockSeq: f.st.SafeWatermark.SafeBlockSeq,
		Indexers:              make([]IndexerTrackView, 0, len(ts.Indexers)),
	}
	for _, it := range ts.Indexers {
		v.Indexers = append(v.Indexers, IndexerTrackView{
			IndexerID:                  it.IndexerID,
			Initial:                    it.Initial,
			QuarantineGeneration:       it.QuarantineGeneration,
			Quarantined:                it.Quarantined,
			QuarantineReason:           it.QuarantineReason,
			RejectedBlocks:             slices.Clone(it.Rejected),
			AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks: slices.Clone(it.Acknowledged),
			PrefixBlockSeq:             f.trackPrefixLocked(it.IndexerID),
			Published:                  f.publishedTrackFrontierLocked(it.IndexerID),
		})
	}
	return v
}

// TracksActivationRefusal is the reason the FSM would refuse the update that
// first sets tracks_enabled on top of the writer and drain gates (contract
// §3.1), or "" when it would not. It is the leader's preflight in the tracks
// gate and changes nothing; Apply decides again.
func (f *FSM) TracksActivationRefusal() string {
	f.mu.RLock()
	defer f.mu.RUnlock()
	return f.tracksActivationRefusalLocked()
}

// TableOwner names the SI indexer that owns tableID's live incarnation
// (contract §3.8): its OwnerIndexerID, or the founding table_registry
// si_indexer_id for an incarnation that carries none. ok is false while the
// registry is disabled and for a table it has never seen. The grouping window
// calls it from ingress handlers under the read lock only, so it never builds
// the derived key index (TableRegistryState.Live may, which is a write).
func (f *FSM) TableOwner(tableID string) (uint64, bool) {
	f.mu.RLock()
	defer f.mu.RUnlock()
	if f.st.Params.TableRegistry == nil {
		return 0, false
	}
	inc := f.st.TableRegistry.liveReadOnly(tableID)
	if inc == nil {
		return 0, false
	}
	return f.incarnationOwnerLocked(inc), true
}

// TrackBlocks lists, ascending, the sealed blocks of track id in (after,
// through]: the blocks a publication that moved the track's entry from after
// to through made safe, which the orchestrator times (contract §3.8). It is
// empty before the tracks activation, when no block has a track.
func (f *FSM) TrackBlocks(id, after, through uint64) []uint64 {
	f.mu.RLock()
	defer f.mu.RUnlock()
	through = min(through, uint64(len(f.st.Blocks)))
	var out []uint64
	for seq := after + 1; seq <= through; seq++ {
		if track, ok := f.blockTrackLocked(seq); ok && track == id {
			out = append(out, seq)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// liveReadOnly answers Live without ever building the derived index: a reader
// holding only f.mu.RLock must not write r.live. With the index present it is
// Live's own lookup; without it, it scans Incarnations newest first under the
// same rule (the newest incarnation that is neither Purged nor Refused, else
// the newest one).
func (r *TableRegistryState) liveReadOnly(key string) *TableIncarnation {
	if r == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if r.live != nil {
		idx := r.live[key]
		if len(idx) == 0 {
			return nil
		}
		for i := len(idx) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
			if inc := r.Incarnations[idx[i]]; inc.Status != TableStatusPurged && inc.Status != TableStatusRefused {
				return inc
			}
		}
		return r.Incarnations[idx[len(idx)-1]]
	}
	var newest *TableIncarnation
	for i := len(r.Incarnations) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		inc := r.Incarnations[i]
		if inc == nil || inc.Key() != key {
			continue
		}
		if newest == nil {
			newest = inc
		}
		if inc.Status != TableStatusPurged && inc.Status != TableStatusRefused {
			return inc
		}
	}
	return newest
}
```

```go
// custodySafeLocked reports whether the published manifest holds blockSeq's
// effects, the condition the orchestrator's custody AUDIT step waits for.
// Before the tracks activation that is the global watermark, as always. After
// it a block is published once its own track's published frontier covers it
// (contract §3.8), which the global watermark may lag while another track is
// stuck; a block without a track is at or below the cutover, which the
// global watermark covers.
func (f *FSM) custodySafeLocked(blockSeq uint64) bool {
	if f.st.SafeWatermark.SafeBlockSeq >= blockSeq {
		return true
	}
	if !f.tracksActiveLocked() {
		return false
	}
	track, ok := f.blockTrackLocked(blockSeq)
	return ok && f.publishedTrackFrontierLocked(track).SafeBlockSeq >= blockSeq
}
```

```go
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"testing"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority/authoritytest"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter/fsm"
)

// enrollServerIndexer2 appends indexer 2 (authoritytest key 1, activation
// block 150, SNode s2, never registered) after the signed-claims activation,
// carrying the committed verifiers, with max_writers 2.
func enrollServerIndexer2(t *testing.T, node *fakeNode) {
	t.Helper()
	view, err := node.f.ConsensusParamsView()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	second := serverEnrolledEntry(t, node.f, authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex1), 2, 150, "s2")
	applyServerUpdate(t, node, func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) {
		u.MaxWriters = 2
		u.SIIndexers = append(slices.Clone(view.Current.SIIndexers), second)
		u.Verifiers = view.Current.Verifiers
	})
}

// enableServerTracks commits the tracks activation directly, carrying every
// committed list (contract §3.1); nothing may be open, unsafe or unpublished.
func enableServerTracks(t *testing.T, node *fakeNode) {
	t.Helper()
	view, err := node.f.ConsensusParamsView()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	applyServerUpdate(t, node, func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) {
		u.MaxWriters = max(view.Current.MaxWriters, 1)
		u.SIIndexers, u.Verifiers, u.TracksEnabled = view.Current.SIIndexers, view.Current.Verifiers, true
	})
	if !node.f.TracksActive() {
		t.Fatal("tracks not active")
	}
}

// activateServerTracks is activateServerSignedClaims (founding indexer 1 on
// the Active SNode s1, verifiers v1..v3, the registry seeded at block 99),
// then the enrolment of indexer 2 and the tracks activation, all bypassing
// the gateway. Nothing is sealed.
func activateServerTracks(t *testing.T, node *fakeNode) {
	t.Helper()
	activateServerSignedClaims(t, node, authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex0))
	enrollServerIndexer2(t, node)
	enableServerTracks(t, node)
}

// serverTableB is db.b, indexer 2's table in these tests.
func serverTableB() payloadexec.TableSchema {
	return payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.b", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "value", Type: "Int64"}}}
}

// addServerTableOfIndexer2 completes block 149, seeds indexer 2 there (the
// unseeded-indexer guard keeps later blocks out until then), adds db.b owned
// by indexer 2 at blocks 150/151 and seals its transition block. db.b stays
// Pending until a manifest publishes that block, and the admission fence lifts
// because indexer 2 now holds its one unpublished transition block.
func addServerTableOfIndexer2(t *testing.T, node *fakeNode) {
	t.Helper()
	two := uint64(2)
	at := func(block uint64) arbiter.L2EventRef {
		return arbiter.L2EventRef{BlockNumber: block, BlockHash: fmt.Sprintf("0x%d", block), TxHash: "0xtx"}
	}
	mustDirectApply(t, node, wire.Command{AdvanceL2Cursor: &wire.AdvanceL2Cursor{To: arbiter.L2BlockRef{Number: 149, Hash: "0x149"}}})
	mustDirectApply(t, node, wire.Command{SeedLegacyTables: &wire.SeedLegacyTables{AtBlock: arbiter.L2BlockRef{Number: 149, Hash: "0x149"}, IndexerID: &two}})
	declared, err := json.Marshal(serverTableB())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	mustDirectApply(t, node, wire.Command{AddTable: &wire.AddTable{DatabaseID: "db", TableID: "b", Created: at(150), Schema: at(151),
		SchemaVersion: 1, SchemaHash: payloadexec.TableSchemaHash(testServerNetworkID, serverTableB()), SchemaJSON: string(declared), OwnerIndexerID: &two}})
	mustDirectApply(t, node, wire.Command{SealL3Block: &wire.SealL3Block{}})
	if node.f.TableSetTransitionPending() {
		t.Fatal("db.b's transition was not sealed")
	}
}

// serverUpdateRequest is the next update over node's current view with every
// committed list and flag carried, edited by mutate, normalized and signed now
// by serverTestAuthority.
func serverUpdateRequest(t *testing.T, node *fakeNode, mutate func(*arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate)) *pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd {
	t.Helper()
	view, err := node.f.ConsensusParamsView()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	u := arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate{
		NetworkID: view.Current.NetworkID, GenesisSnapshotID: view.GenesisSnapshotID, ExpectedEpoch: view.Epoch,
		PreviousParamsDigest: view.ParamsDigest, AuthorityAddresses: view.Current.AuthorityAddresses, MaxWriters: max(view.Current.MaxWriters, 1),
		ExpectedPromotionSeq: view.PromotionSeq, TableRegistry: view.Current.TableRegistry, ClientLanes: view.Current.ClientLanes,
		SIIndexers: view.Current.SIIndexers, Verifiers: view.Current.Verifiers, TracksEnabled: view.Current.TracksEnabled,
	}
	mutate(&u)
	u, err = authority.NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(u)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	token, err := serverTestAuthority.SignConsensusParamsUpdate(u)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return &pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd{Update: wire.ConsensusParamsUpdateToPB(u), AuthorityJws: token}
}

// serverTracksActivationRequest is the tracks activation over node's current
// view.
func serverTracksActivationRequest(t *testing.T, node *fakeNode) *pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd {
	t.Helper()
	return serverUpdateRequest(t, node, func(u *arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) { u.TracksEnabled = true })
}

// signedSNodeRegistration is SNode node's registration at seq advertising
// features, signed by signer over the registration exactly as Apply decodes
// it from the log.
func signedSNodeRegistration(t *testing.T, f *fsm.FSM, signer *authority.Signer, node string, seq uint64, features ...string) *pb.NodeRegistration {
	t.Helper()
	req := wire.RegistrationToPB(arbiter.NodeRegistration{NodeID: node, Roles: []arbiter.NodeRole{arbiter.NodeRoleSNode}, RegistrationSeq: seq})
	jws, err := signer.SignSNodeMessage(authority.SNodeMessageRegistration, serverMessageContext(t, f), wire.RegistrationFromPB(req))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	req.SignerJws, req.Features = jws, features
	return req
}

// quarantineRequest is the QuarantineIndexer request for (id, generation,
// reason), signed now by signer under f's current authority context.
func quarantineRequest(t *testing.T, f *fsm.FSM, signer *authority.Signer, id, generation uint64, reason string) *pb.QuarantineIndexerCmd {
	t.Helper()
	token, err := signer.SignQuarantineIndexerWithContext(
		arbiter.QuarantineIndexerCommand{IndexerID: id, ExpectedGeneration: generation, Reason: reason}, serverAuthorityContext(t, f))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return &pb.QuarantineIndexerCmd{IndexerId: id, ExpectedGeneration: generation, Reason: reason, AuthorityJws: token}
}

// releaseRequest is the ReleaseIndexer request for (id, generation,
// acknowledged), signed now by signer over the canonical list.
func releaseRequest(t *testing.T, f *fsm.FSM, signer *authority.Signer, id, generation uint64, acknowledged ...uint64) *pb.ReleaseIndexerCmd {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.ReleaseIndexer{IndexerID: id, ExpectedGeneration: generation, AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks: acknowledged}
	token, err := signer.SignReleaseIndexerWithContext(cmd.Canonical(), serverAuthorityContext(t, f))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return &pb.ReleaseIndexerCmd{IndexerId: id, ExpectedGeneration: generation, AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks: acknowledged, AuthorityJws: token}
}

// quarantineCommand and releaseCommand are those requests, signed by
// serverTestAuthority, as Raft commands for direct application.
func quarantineCommand(t *testing.T, f *fsm.FSM, id, generation uint64, reason string) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.QuarantineIndexerFromRequest(quarantineRequest(t, f, serverTestAuthority, id, generation, reason))
	return wire.Command{QuarantineIndexer: &cmd}
}

func releaseCommand(t *testing.T, f *fsm.FSM, id, generation uint64) wire.Command {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := wire.ReleaseIndexerFromRequest(releaseRequest(t, f, serverTestAuthority, id, generation))
	return wire.Command{ReleaseIndexer: &cmd}
}

// prepareTracksGate registers SNode s1 (advertising s1Features) and verifiers
// v1..v3 (every local feature) through s's gateway, so s's feature book holds
// them, activates s1 before the signed-claims activation, and commits that
// activation directly on vn. Nothing is sealed, so the tracks activation's
// FSM preconditions hold.
func prepareTracksGate(t *testing.T, s *Server, vn voterNode, s1Features ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	enableServerTableRegistry(t, vn.fakeNode)
	ctx := context.Background()
	m := &membershipService{s: s}
	for _, req := range []*pb.NodeRegistration{
		{NodeId: "s1", Roles: []pb.NodeRole{pb.NodeRole_NODE_ROLE_SNODE}, Features: s1Features},
		verifierRequest("v1", 1, arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()...),
		verifierRequest("v2", 2, arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()...),
		verifierRequest("v3", 3, arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()...),
	} {
		if _, err := m.RegisterNode(ctx, req); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("register %s: %v", req.GetNodeId(), err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := m.MarkActive(ctx, &pb.NodeRef{NodeId: "s1"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("activate s1: %v", err)
	}
	req := serverActivationRequest(t, vn.fakeNode, authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex0))
	mustDirectApply(t, vn.fakeNode, wire.Command{UpdateConsensusParams: &wire.UpdateConsensusParams{
		Update: wire.ConsensusParamsUpdateFromPB(req.GetUpdate()), AuthorityJWS: req.GetAuthorityJws()}})
	if !vn.f.SignedClaimsActive() {
		t.Fatal("signed claims not active")
	}
}
```
