```go
// TrackState is the replicated stage-2 state (spec §7.4–§7.6). It exists
// exactly when Params.TracksEnabled is committed.
type TrackState struct {
	// Cutover is the sealed tip and PromotionSeq when the activation applied.
	Cutover TrackCutover `json:"cutover"`
	// Indexers has one entry per si_indexers entry, sorted by indexer id.
	Indexers []IndexerTrack `json:"indexers"`
	// RejectedParts are the candidate parts of acknowledged rejected blocks
	// that still await their cleanup (clarification C4), sorted by
	// (block, table, partition).
	RejectedParts []RejectedPartition `json:"rejected_parts,omitempty"`
}

// TrackCutover is the activation point (spec §7.6).
type TrackCutover struct {
	BlockSeq     uint64 `json:"block_seq"`
	PromotionSeq uint64 `json:"promotion_seq"`
}

// IndexerTrack is one SI indexer's track state.
type IndexerTrack struct {
	IndexerID uint64 `json:"indexer_id"`
	// Initial is the track's frontier before its first own block: the cutover
	// for an indexer enrolled at the activation, {global prefix, PromotionSeq}
	// at its enrolment commit for one enrolled later (spec §7.6).
	Initial replay.TrackFrontier `json:"initial"`
	// QuarantineGeneration starts at 0 and is incremented by every applied
	// quarantine, release and automatic quarantine (spec §7.4).
	QuarantineGeneration uint64 `json:"quarantine_generation"`
	Quarantined          bool   `json:"quarantined,omitempty"`
	QuarantineReason     string `json:"quarantine_reason,omitempty"`
	// Rejected lists this track's rejected blocks a release has not yet
	// acknowledged; Acknowledged lists those it has (spec §7.5). Both ascending.
	Rejected     []uint64 `json:"rejected,omitempty"`
	Acknowledged []uint64 `json:"acknowledged,omitempty"`
}

// RejectedPartition is the cleanup work of one acknowledged rejected block in
// one partition (clarification C4): Parts not yet acknowledged as dropped,
// and the scheduled cleanup once ScheduleUnsafeCleanup recorded it.
type RejectedPartition struct {
	BlockSeq       uint64                 `json:"block_seq"`
	TableID        string                 `json:"table_id"`
	PartitionID    string                 `json:"partition_id"`
	Parts          []arbiter.PartRef      `json:"parts"`
	Scheduled      *arbiter.UnsafeCleanup `json:"scheduled,omitempty"`
	AuthorityJWS   string                 `json:"authority_jws,omitempty"`
	AuthorityEpoch uint64                 `json:"authority_epoch,omitempty"`
}
```

Helpers (names verbatim; the caller holds `f.mu`):
- `(f *FSM) tracksActiveLocked() bool { return f.st.Params.TracksEnabled }` and the reader `(f *FSM) TracksActive() bool`.
- `(f *FSM) indexerTrackLocked(id uint64) *IndexerTrack` — nil when `Tracks` is nil or the id has no entry.
- `(f *FSM) blockTrackLocked(blockSeq uint64) (uint64, bool)` — the header's `Track.IndexerID`; false for a block without a track.
- `(f *FSM) incarnationOwnerLocked(inc *TableIncarnation) uint64` — `*inc.OwnerIndexerID`, or `Params.TableRegistry.SIIndexerID` when nil (the stage-1 founding rule, shared with `ownerSourceLocked`).
- `(f *FSM) manifestTableOwnerLocked(tableID string) (uint64, bool)` — the owner of the newest incarnation of `tableID` that is not Refused and that ever entered a table set (`Origin == TableOriginGenesis || AddBlockSeq != 0`); false when there is none. By spec D9 and `RefusedPreviousIncarnationNotPurged`, a table key in any manifest has exactly that incarnation.
- `(f *FSM) statementTrackLocked(seq uint64) (uint64, bool)` — the track of the statement's sealed block; `(f *FSM) promotionTrackLocked(promotionSeq uint64) (uint64, bool)` — the shared track of `PendingPromotions[seq].StatementSeqs` (false when they disagree or none is sealed).
- `(f *FSM) blockPassedLocked(blockSeq uint64) bool` — a transition block: `transitionBlockSafe`; a block whose track's `Acknowledged` lists it: true; otherwise every statement Safe (via `blockStatementsComplete`, a short list is not passed). Before the activation `Acknowledged` is empty everywhere, so this is today's predicate.
- `safePrefixLocked(f)` becomes the contiguous prefix of `blockPassedLocked` (clarification C3); behaviour before the activation is unchanged.
- `(f *FSM) trackPrefixLocked(id uint64) uint64` — start from `indexerTrackLocked(id).Initial.SafeBlockSeq`, walk blocks above it in order, skip blocks of other tracks, advance over each passed block of track `id`, stop at the first one that is not passed.
- `(f *FSM) nextTrackBlockLocked(id, after uint64) (uint64, bool)` — the first block of track `id` above `after`.
- `(f *FSM) publishedTrackFrontierLocked(id uint64) replay.TrackFrontier` — the entry for `id` in the latest published manifest's `TrackFrontiers`, else the track's `Initial` (the manifest published before the activation has no entries).
- `(f *FSM) trackInDebtLocked(id uint64) bool` — `trackPrefixLocked(id) > publishedTrackFrontierLocked(id).SafeBlockSeq`.
- `(f *FSM) indexerQuarantinedLocked(id uint64) bool`.

#### 3.1 Tracks activation (Task 6)

- `verifyConsensusTransition` (signed history, also replayed by restore): `tracks_enabled` may go false→true only when `len(previous.SIIndexers) > 0` (clarification C11; error `consensus update cannot enable tracks before the signed-claims activation`); true→false is refused (`consensus update must carry tracks_enabled once set`).
- `applyUpdateConsensusParams` (committed state), for the update that first sets it, `tracksActivationRefusalLocked() string`, checked after the existing writer gate and drain gate and before any mutation, refuses unless, in this order: the open block is empty (`tracks activation requires an empty open block`); `safePrefixLocked(f) == uint64(len(f.st.Blocks))` (`tracks activation requires every sealed block to be safe`); `f.st.SafeWatermark.SafeBlockSeq == uint64(len(f.st.Blocks))` (`tracks activation requires the published manifest to cover the sealed tip`); `f.st.ArtifactDisposition.Capability == 0` (`tracks activation requires artifact disposition capability 0`); the snapshot-query reservation barrier is idle (`tracks activation requires an idle snapshot-query barrier`).
- Applying it sets `f.st.Tracks = &TrackState{Cutover: {BlockSeq: len(Blocks), PromotionSeq: f.st.PromotionSeq}, Indexers: one IndexerTrack per si_indexers entry with Initial = {IndexerID: id, SafeBlockSeq: cutover.BlockSeq, AppliedPromotionSeq: cutover.PromotionSeq}}`. The registry view does not change, so the activation does not bump it.
- After the activation an update that appends an si_indexers entry adds its `IndexerTrack` with `Initial = {id, safePrefixLocked(f), f.st.PromotionSeq}` in the same Apply, after the new params are in place (spec §7.6).
- After the activation `applyUpdateConsensusParams` refuses raising `artifact_disposition_capability` (`artifact disposition capability cannot be raised while tracks are enabled`), and `applyBeginSnapshotQuery` refuses with `snapshot-query lane is not track-aware; refused while tracks are enabled` before any mutation (clarification C7).

#### 3.2 One owner per block (Task 7)

- `applySealL3Block` is split into `(f *FSM) prepareStatementSealLocked(spentIDsRoot string) (*preparedSeal, string)` (no mutation; builds the header, including `Track` from `OpenBlock.Owner` after the activation, and proves its chain hash) and `(f *FSM) commitSealLocked(p *preparedSeal) SealResult` (stamps statements, collects sources, appends the header and its `BlockVerification`, increments `NextL3BlockSeq`, resets `OpenBlock` with `Owner == nil`, emits `EventBlockSealed`). `applySealL3Block` calls both with the current spent-ids root; its output before the activation is byte-identical.
- `fillSealedHeaderChainFieldsLocked(h *L3BlockHeader, spentIDsRoot string) error` takes the root it stamps instead of reading `SpentIDs` itself; every existing caller passes `"0x" + hex.EncodeToString(f.st.SpentIDs.Root())`.
- Admission after the activation, with `owner := f.incarnationOwnerLocked(live)`: quarantine (§3.5) is checked immediately before the owner-source check; after the lane budget and before `SpentIDs.Insert`, when the open block is non-empty and `*OpenBlock.Owner != owner`, it calls `prepareStatementSealLocked` with the pre-insert root (a refusal returns `Rejected{Reason: "owner switch seal: " + reason}` with state unchanged), then inserts, and only if the insert succeeded commits the seal (clarification C10). The statement then opens or joins the open block, which records `Owner = &owner`. `SubmitResult` is unchanged.
- A statement block sealed after the activation carries `L3BlockTrack{IndexerID: *OpenBlock.Owner}`; a nil owner on a non-empty open block after the activation is refused (`open block has no owner`).
- Transition blocks: `pendingTableSetChangesLocked` groups changes by `incarnationOwnerLocked`; after the activation `plannedTableSetTransitionLocked` plans for the lowest owner id that has changes, no unpublished transition block of its own (a transition block of that track above `publishedTrackFrontierLocked(owner).SafeBlockSeq`) and a change set that applies to the published base; the plan carries that owner and the sealed header carries `L3BlockTrack{IndexerID: owner}`. Before the activation the global rule (at most one unpublished transition block, all owners in one block) is unchanged. The admission fence and `TableSetTransitionUnsealable` keep their meaning: the fence holds while any owner's plan is sealable now; `TableSetTransitionUnsealable` reports the lowest owner whose change does not fit the base.

#### 3.3 Per-track progress (Task 8)

- `applyRecordPromotionIssued` after the activation: `t, ok := promotionTrackLocked`-style resolution over the covered statements (refuse when they span tracks or one is unsealed); refuse while `indexerQuarantinedLocked(t)` (`indexer <t> is quarantined; no new promotion is issued`); replace the global debt gate with `trackInDebtLocked(t)` (`safe prefix of indexer <t> awaits manifest publication before new promotions`); replace the global frontier with `nextTrackBlockLocked(t, trackPrefixLocked(t))` (`promotion covers statements beyond the safe-prefix frontier of indexer <t>`). Before the activation the global rules are unchanged.
- `WorkSet` after the activation: `PromotablePending` skips a statement whose track is quarantined or in debt or whose block is beyond its track's frontier; `NeedManifest` is true when any enrolled track is in debt; `PublishedUncleaned` takes a promotion only when its maximum block is at or below `publishedTrackFrontierLocked(t).SafeBlockSeq` and `t` is not quarantined (clarification C5); `IssuedUnacked` and `ScheduledUnackedCleanups` omit quarantined tracks (clarification C8). Before the activation every field is computed exactly as today.
- `WorkSet` gains `Tracks []TrackWork` (empty before the activation), sorted by indexer id: `TrackWork{IndexerID, Prefix uint64, Published replay.TrackFrontier, Quarantined bool, QuarantineGeneration uint64}` — read by metrics and the orchestrator.

#### 3.4 Track-aware manifest (Task 9)

- `ManifestInputs` gains `TrackFrontiers []replay.TrackFrontier`. After the activation `manifestInputsLocked` returns `trackManifestInputsLocked(f)`; before it, today's function unchanged.
- `trackManifestInputsLocked`: parent = the manifest of `SafeWatermark.SnapshotID`; each parent table is classified by `manifestTableOwnerLocked` (a table without an enrolled owner makes the inputs incomplete); for each si_indexers entry in id order, with `base` = the parent's entry for that id, else `Initial`: **Advanced** when `trackPrefixLocked(id) > base.SafeBlockSeq` — entry `{id, prefix, f.st.PromotionSeq}`, tables = the parent's tables of that owner with that track's transition blocks in `(base.SafeBlockSeq, prefix]` applied in block order through `resultSet` (adds enter empty, retires leave), then every live `Partitions` / `SafeParts` entry of that owner's tables overlaid exactly as today's overlay does; **Carried** when the parent has an entry — that entry and the parent's tables of that owner verbatim; **Initialised** otherwise — `Initial` and the parent's tables of that owner verbatim. No Advanced track → no inputs (`ok == false`). `SafeBlockSeq = safePrefixLocked(f)`; `SchemaRoot = payloadexec.SchemaRootFromHashes` over every resulting table (clarification C1); `TrackFrontiers` sorted by id.
- `validateManifestPublication` after the activation: `manifest.Validate()`; identity checks as today; parent equals the watermark; `SafeBlockSeq == safePrefixLocked(f)` and `>= parent.SafeBlockSeq` (clarification C6); `TrackFrontiers` names exactly the enrolled indexers; each entry `>=` its base on both fields, `SafeBlockSeq >= Tracks.Cutover.BlockSeq`, and `>=` the track's last block at or below the manifest's `SafeBlockSeq`; at least one entry advanced; finally the recomputed `trackManifestInputsLocked` sealed through `replay.SafeSnapshotManifest.Seal()` must have the same `ManifestRoot`. Every refusal names the first failing rule.
- `applyPublishSafeSnapshot` after the activation stores the manifest, sets `SafeWatermark` from it, and runs `applyPublishedTrackTransitionsLocked(parent, manifest)`: per track, every transition block of that track in `(base.SafeBlockSeq, entry.SafeBlockSeq]` flips its adds Pending→Active and its retires Retiring→Purging and drops the retired tables' `Partitions` and `SafeParts`; one registry bump when anything flipped. Before the activation `applyPublishedTableSetTransitionsLocked` is unchanged.

#### 3.5 Quarantine and release (Task 10)

- Wire commands `wire.QuarantineIndexer` and `wire.ReleaseIndexer` (Appendix A §2). Apply refuses before the tracks activation (`quarantine requires the tracks activation`), then requires an si_indexers entry for the id, then verifies the authority JWS with `(&authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: authorityAddressSet(Params.AuthorityAddresses)}).VerifyQuarantineIndexer` / `VerifyReleaseIndexer` under the exact `authority.ConsensusContext{NetworkID, GenesisSnapshotID, AuthorityEpoch: f.st.ConsensusEpoch}`, then requires `ExpectedGeneration == QuarantineGeneration` (`expected_generation <n> differs from quarantine generation <m> of indexer <id>`).
- Quarantine: refused when already quarantined; sets `Quarantined`, `QuarantineReason`, increments the generation.
- Release: refused when not quarantined; `AcknowledgedRejectedBlocks` must equal the track's `Rejected` exactly (sorted, unique; `release must acknowledge exactly the rejected blocks <list>`); moves them to `Acknowledged`, records their rejected parts (§3.6), clears `Quarantined` and the reason, increments the generation.
- Automatic quarantine: when `applyResolveChallenge` with verdict Rejected changed at least one statement of a block with a track, after the activation, that block joins the track's `Rejected`, the track is quarantined with reason `block <n> rejected`, and the generation increments, whether or not it was already quarantined.
- Each of the three bumps the registry once (the view carries the quarantined set) and emits `EventIndexerQuarantineChanged`.
- Admission: `SubmitResult{Code: arbiter.AdmissionCodeIndexerQuarantined, Message: "storage-integrity indexer <id> is quarantined"}`, state unchanged, checked immediately before the owner-source check (clarification C9).
- `applyScheduleUnsafeCleanup` refuses a cleanup of a quarantined track (`indexer <t> is quarantined; no new cleanup is scheduled`), the track resolved through `promotionTrackLocked(cleanup.PromotionSeq)` or, for a rejected-part cleanup, the block's track.
- Drain gate after the activation: an unacknowledged promotion, a pending cleanup, a promoted unsafe part and a rejected partition count only when their track is not quarantined; tracks resolve through `promotionTrackLocked`, the cleanup's promotion, `manifestTableOwnerLocked(table)` for `PromotedUnsafe`, and `RejectedPartition.BlockSeq` respectively.
- `TableRegistryView` gains `QuarantinedIndexers []uint64` (ascending), served as `TableRegistrySnapshot.quarantined_indexers`.

#### 3.6 Rejected-part cleanup (Task 11)

- A release that acknowledges block `b` appends, for every partition in which a Rejected statement of `b` has a bound RC candidate part still in `UnpromotedParts`, one `RejectedPartition{BlockSeq: b, TableID, PartitionID, Parts}` (parts sorted by `PartRowLtHash`).
- `WorkSet` gains `RejectedUncleaned []CleanupWork` (unscheduled partitions of tracks that are not quarantined, `Cleanup{TableID, PartitionID, PromotionSeq: 0, RejectedBlockSeq: b, Parts}`) and `ScheduledRejectedCleanups []CleanupWork` (scheduled, not yet acknowledged, tracks not quarantined).
- `applyScheduleUnsafeCleanup` with `Cleanup.RejectedBlockSeq != 0`: refused before the tracks activation and when `PromotionSeq != 0`; verifies the authority JWS over `authority.CleanupCommandHash` like every cleanup; requires a recorded `RejectedPartition` for `(b, table, partition)` whose `Parts` are exactly the command's parts; records `Scheduled`, `AuthorityJWS`, `AuthorityEpoch`; an identical re-schedule is a no-op.
- `applyRecordCleanupAck` with `Ack.RejectedBlockSeq != 0`: the expected source is the shared bound `SourceNode` of block `b`'s Rejected statements; the ack must name it and carry its SNode signature (`SNodeMessageCleanupAck` over the ack); it deletes that `RejectedPartition`. An acknowledgement for a partition already deleted is an idempotent no-op.
- `(f *FSM) RejectedCleanupSource(blockSeq uint64) (string, error)` is the orchestrator's routing read (same rule as the acknowledgement). Task 11 also wires the orchestrator: `ws.RejectedUncleaned` is scheduled through `ScheduleUnsafeCleanup` (authority-signed like `scheduleCleanup`), and `ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups` is streamed to `RejectedCleanupSource` and re-signed on every rescan like `streamCleanupSigned`.

#### 3.7 Snapshot v20 (Task 12)

- `snapshotVersion = 20`, `snapshotVersionV20 = 20`; `snapshotWriteVersion` returns 20 exactly when `st.Params.TracksEnabled`. `snapshotDoc` gains `Tracks *TrackState `json:"tracks,omitempty"``.
- Restore refuses, under a version byte below 20: `Params.TracksEnabled` or `BootstrapParams.TracksEnabled`, a present `tracks` member, any header with `Track`, an open block with `Owner` (`tracks state is present in a pre-v20 container`).
- `validateTrackState(st *State) error` (restore): `TracksEnabled` iff `Tracks != nil`; `Indexers` are exactly the si_indexers ids, ascending; every `Initial.SafeBlockSeq >= Cutover.BlockSeq` and `Initial.AppliedPromotionSeq >= Cutover.PromotionSeq`; blocks at or below the cutover have no track and every later block names an enrolled indexer; a transition block's adds and retires are all owned by its track; the open block has an owner iff it is non-empty after the activation, and it names an enrolled indexer; `Rejected` and `Acknowledged` are ascending, disjoint, name blocks of that track holding a Rejected statement; a quarantined track's reason is non-empty; every `RejectedPartition` names an acknowledged block of a track and a non-empty sorted part list. Keys are visited in sorted order so every replica names the same corruption.

#### 3.8 Server and orchestrator (Task 13)

- **Reads the services need (fsm, `f.mu.RLock`, never writing the lazy registry index):** `(f *FSM) TableOwner(tableID string) (uint64, bool)` — the live incarnation's owner (founding rule for nil), false when the registry is disabled or the table is unknown; when `TableRegistryState.live` is nil it scans `Incarnations` instead of rebuilding the index. `(f *FSM) TrackStateView() TrackStateView` — the data of `pb.TrackStateView` (cutover, global prefix, published global seq, per indexer: initial, generation, quarantined, reason, rejected, acknowledged, `trackPrefixLocked`, `publishedTrackFrontierLocked`); zero value before the activation. `(f *FSM) TracksActivationRefusal() string` — `tracksActivationRefusalLocked` under the read lock (the leader's preflight; Apply decides again).
- **ConsensusAdmin `QuarantineIndexer` / `ReleaseIndexer`** live beside `EvictNode` in `server/signed_messages.go` and keep its check order: consensus updates enabled; `FailedPrecondition` `quarantine requires the tracks activation` before it; shape (`reason` non-empty for a quarantine; the release list strictly ascending); `consensusLeaderCheck`; the `ConsensusParamsView` context (`network_id`, genesis snapshot id, `epoch`); `authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: current authority set, MaxTokenAge: cfg}.AuthorizeQuarantineIndexer` / `AuthorizeReleaseIndexer`; `s.propose(wire.Command{QuarantineIndexer: …})`; an FSM `Rejected` maps to `FailedPrecondition` carrying its reason. `GetTrackState` runs `consensusReadBarrier` and answers `TrackStateView` (followers answer `NotLeader` like `GetConsensusParams`).
- **Tracks gate** (`server/tracks_gate.go`, `(s *Server) tracksGate(ctx, update arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate) error`), called from `UpdateConsensusParams` exactly where `signedClaimsGate` is, under `membershipMu.Lock()` + `consensusReadBarrier` when the update first sets `tracks_enabled`: refuse while non-voters exist; refuse with the FSM's `TracksActivationRefusal()` reason when non-empty; refuse unless every `PurgeNodeSet()` node has `features.answer(id, CurrentTerm())` containing `track_manifests_v1` (`tracks gate refused: data-plane nodes <ids> have not registered with this leader advertising track_manifests_v1; restart them on a stage-2 release`).
- **Membership after the activation:** `RegisterNode` refuses a data-plane registration whose features lack `track_manifests_v1` with `FailedPrecondition` `tracks are active; this binary does not support track-aware manifests` (beside the two existing refusals in `server/membership.go`).
- **Promotion gateway:** before the activation `AckCleanup` refuses `rejected_block_seq != 0` with `InvalidArgument` without proposing.
- **Dispatch:** quarantine suppression is the `WorkSet` filter (contract §3.3, C8); `promotionTargets` is unchanged. (Task 11 owns this rejected-cleanup orchestration, not Task 13:) the orchestrator streams `ws.ScheduledRejectedCleanups` to `FSM.RejectedCleanupSource(blockSeq)` with the same re-signing path as `streamCleanupSigned`, and schedules `ws.RejectedUncleaned` through `ScheduleUnsafeCleanup` like `PublishedUncleaned`. An `EventIndexerQuarantineChanged` triggers a rescan (any non-Admitted event does), so a release re-dispatches suspended work on the next pass.
- **Seal loop:** the transition branch of `orchestrator/seal.go` repeats "seal the open block if non-empty, then seal a transition" while `TableSetTransitionPending()` stays true, bounded by the number of enrolled indexers plus one per pass. Seal times are recorded from `EventBlockSealed` (so owner-switch seals inside admission are timed), not only around the orchestrator's own proposals.
- **Publication metrics:** after the activation `observePublishedBlocks` observes, for every track entry that advanced, the blocks of that track in `(old entry, new entry]`; before it, unchanged. The `safe watermark advanced` log line also names the advanced tracks.
- **Custody:** after the activation a block's custody work is Safe when its track's published frontier covers it (`CustodyWork.Safe`), not the global watermark.
- **Grouping window** (`server.Config.SubmissionGroupingWindow time.Duration`; zero = off, the value of every existing construction site): after the activation, on the leader, `SubmitStatement` hands its command to a server-owned grouper instead of proposing it directly. The grouper opens a window when a submission arrives while none is held and closes it `SubmissionGroupingWindow` later; at close it proposes the held commands from one goroutine through the existing `proposeTracked`, grouped by `FSM.TableOwner(env.TargetTableID)` — owners in the order of their first held submission, arrival order within an owner, unresolvable owners last — and hands each handler its own result. Followers, and every submission before the activation, take today's path unchanged. `OnLeadershipLost` and `Close` fail the held submissions with the same `NotLeader` error a follower returns. Config: `ingress.submission_grouping_window` (YAML duration; raw pointer default `50ms`; explicit `0` disables and is the one duration `Validate` accepts at zero); plumbed through `cmd/arbiter/services.go`.
- **Read APIs:** `l3HeaderToPB` copies `Track` (proto field 14). `TableRegistry.GetTableRegistry` / `WatchTableRegistry` serve `quarantined_indexers`.
- **Metrics** (custom collector over `fsm.MetricsSnapshot()`, which gains a per-indexer track list): `arbiter_track_safe_block_seq{indexer_id}`, `arbiter_track_published_block_seq{indexer_id}`, `arbiter_track_quarantined{indexer_id}` (0/1), `arbiter_track_quarantine_generation{indexer_id}`; emitted only after the activation. The README metric policy names the exception: `indexer_id` labels only enrolled SI indexers, a governed, bounded set.

#### 3.9 arbiter-admin (Task 14)

- `arbiter-admin consensus update … --tracks-enabled` sets `TracksEnabled`; after the activation every update carries it whether or not the flag is given (like `--client-lanes-max-per-account`). When the update first sets it, the CLI runs a third activation gate before signing: every `--voter`'s `GetProtocolInfo.features` contains `track_manifests_v1`, every `GetNodeFeatures` entry advertises it, and `GetTrackState` answers `tracks_enabled: false`; the leader's gate (§3.8) decides again.
- `arbiter-admin consensus tracks --address <leader>` prints `GetTrackState` as JSON (protojson, `UseProtoNames`, `EmitUnpopulated`).
- `arbiter-admin indexer quarantine --address <leader> --indexer <id> --expected-generation <n> --reason <text>` and `arbiter-admin indexer release --address <leader> --indexer <id> --expected-generation <n> [--acknowledge-rejected <block>]…` copy `node evict`: authority key from `ARBITER_AUTHORITY_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX` only, context from a barriered `GetConsensusParams`, outcome-unknown error codes mapped as `node evict` maps them, JSON output `{indexer_id, expected_generation, …, outcome}`.
- `consensus show` needs no code change: protojson prints `tracks_enabled` once arbiter-proto carries it.

Every existing integration test passes unchanged (pre-activation behaviour).

### 6. Release ledger names and commands

- Ledger: `PROTO_TAG` (Task 1), `HG_TAG` (Task 3), `CORE_TAG` (Task 5), `ARBITER_TAG` / `ARBITER_DIGEST` (Task 15); Plan S2-B: `SN_COMMIT` / `SN_DIGEST` (Task 16).

- housegate, arbiter-core, arbiter: `bazel build //... && bazel test //...`; after dependency changes `bazel mod tidy && bazel run //:gazelle`. housegate pins arbiter-proto with `GOWORK=off go get github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto@$PROTO_TAG && GOWORK=off go mod tidy && bazel mod tidy && bazel run //:gazelle`. arbiter-core pins arbiter-proto the same way and housegate with `bash scripts/update-housegate.sh $HG_TAG`. arbiter pins arbiter-core with `bash scripts/update-arbiter-core.sh $CORE_TAG` and housegate with `bash scripts/update-housegate.sh $HG_TAG`.
- One URWT worktree per repository at `~/src/remotesrc/claude/<repo>/multi-source-s2`, branch `urwt/claude/multi-source-s2`, created with the URWT command (agents: `$W` = that worktree; prefix each Bash call with `W=<path>;`).
- Commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Code comments in English. Markdown never hard-wrapped.
- TDD: every task step is failing test → run (fail) → minimal implementation → run (pass) → commit, in each repository's existing test style.

### 7. Amendments after drafting (binding)

These amendments resolve the contract conflicts the drafting groups recorded (Appendix B). They supersede the sections above where they differ, and every task is drafted to them.

- **A1 (G1-2) — the header field lands with the pin.** Pinning `CORE_TAG` in Task 6 pulls `PROTO_TAG` into arbiter, and `TestL3BlockHeaderMirrorsProto` (`server/safestate_l3block_test.go:65-85`) then requires `fsm.L3BlockHeader.Track`. Task 6 therefore adds `fsm.L3BlockTrack` and the nil, `omitempty` `L3BlockHeader.Track` field (nothing writes it yet) together with the pin; Task 7 starts setting it.
- **A2 (G2-1) — where the canonical commands live.** `arbiter.QuarantineIndexerCommand` and `arbiter.ReleaseIndexerCommand` are declared in arbiter-core `consensus.go`, beside `EvictNodeCommand` (not `types.go`).
- **A3 (G2-2) — the quarantined set names enrolled indexers.** `wire.TableRegistrySnapshotFromPB` refuses a `quarantined_indexers` id without an `si_indexers` entry, as it does for `seeded_indexers`.
- **A4 (G2-3, G2-4) — new frozen fixtures.** arbiter-core `wire/tracks_golden_test.go` (pre-tracks Raft bytes of `ScheduleUnsafeCleanup` and `PublishSafeSnapshot`), `authority/tracks_golden_test.go` (the pre-tracks cleanup hash) and the new `authority/authoritytest/tracks.go` vectors join the frozen-fixture list; the existing `authoritytest` vector files stay untouched.
- **A5 (G2-5, G2-6, G2-7, G2-8) — signing and converter details.** `authority` also exports `SignQuarantineIndexerWithContextAt` / `SignReleaseIndexerWithContextAt` (explicit issue time, for vectors). `ReleaseIndexerHash` validates the list (strictly ascending) and never sorts; `wire.ReleaseIndexer.Canonical()` is the only normaliser; `QuarantineIndexerCommand` with a blank reason is refused. `wire` also exports `QuarantineIndexerToRequest`, `ReleaseIndexerToRequest`, `TrackFrontierFromPB` and `TrackFrontierToPB` (Task 13 uses the last two for `GetTrackState`).
- **A6 (G2-9) — the verifier's proof point.** "The verifier replays against track-aware manifests" is proven at the manifest store (`dataplane/manifests.go`), the verifier's only manifest decode point; `snode/claims.go` and `verifier/claims.go` need no change.
- **A7 (G5-1, clarification C14) — restore keeps quarantined work across epochs.** `validateConsensusHistory` (`fsm/consensus_history.go:75-77`, `:132-134`) refuses an unacknowledged promotion or a pending cleanup whose authority epoch is not the current one ("belongs to a drained authority epoch"). After the tracks activation a consensus update may commit while a quarantined track still holds such work (spec §7.4), so that rule would make every later snapshot unrestorable. Resolution: let `tracksWorkEpochFloor` be the epoch that follows the update which first set `tracks_enabled` (derived from `ConsensusUpdates`; none before the activation); an unacknowledged promotion or a pending cleanup whose authority epoch is at or above that floor is accepted at restore even when it is older than the current epoch. Its authority proof is still verified against the parameters of its own epoch, and every pre-floor rule is unchanged. Task 10 implements it; Task 12 validates `RejectedPartition.AuthorityJWS` / `AuthorityEpoch` the same way.
- **A8 (G5-2, G2-6) — a quarantine needs a reason.** Apply refuses a `QuarantineIndexer` whose reason is blank (restore refuses a quarantined track without a reason).
- **A9 (G5-3, G5-4) — refusal strings and rejected-cleanup details.** The quarantine, release and rejected-cleanup refusal strings that Appendix A leaves open are the ones Tasks 10–11 fix verbatim. A rejected-part cleanup and its acknowledgement are refused by Apply before the activation; its acknowledgement must carry `promotion_seq == 0`; an acknowledgement for a recorded but unscheduled partition is refused, one for an unrecorded partition is a no-op; a release of an incomplete block is refused; rejected-part cleanups never enter `PendingCleanups` or `CleanupAudits` (their proof lives on the `RejectedPartition`).
- **A10 (G7-1) — quarantine dominates readiness on the host.** sentio-node's `evaluate` resolves the schema, then applies the quarantine rule, then readiness: an Active incarnation of a quarantined host answers Refused (with its schema) even before it is ready.
- **A11 (G7-2) — the devnet2 stuck track is best effort.** devnet2 seals within `seal.max_age` 2 s and reaches safe about 4.8 s later, and nothing suspends one indexer alone, so the runbook writes one indexer-b row and quiesces indexer-b in the same block, then requires the block to be sealed but not safe (global prefix and `hg_safe` rows unchanged) before it checks indexer-a's track; one retry is allowed; if both attempts miss the window, Plan S2-A Task 15's `TestTwoTracksStoppingOneSNodeStallsOnlyItsTrack` is the recorded proof and the live step is marked "not reproduced".
- **A12 (G7-3) — quarantine is exercised on a running indexer-b.** The live order is: stuck track → restore indexer-b and converge → quarantine and release while indexer-b runs (host-side checks exec into its pod and its HouseGate serves the refused INSERT).
- **A13 (G7 facts) — CLI shape the runbook relies on.** `arbiter-admin consensus update` accepts `--voter` together with `--tracks-enabled` (today only with lanes or `--si-indexer`, `cmd/arbiter-admin/main.go:369-411`); `indexer quarantine` / `indexer release` accept `--timeout` like `node evict`.
- **A14 (G4-1) — restore walks track-aware manifests.** `validateRestoredManifestsWalk` (`fsm/genesis_validation.go:134-167`) refuses a child labelled with its parent's `safe_block_seq` (allowed by C6) and two tracks' transitions pinned to one base (allowed by C1). After the activation restore uses `validateRestoredTrackManifest` instead, which re-derives each track-aware manifest with Task 9's rules; pre-activation manifests keep the existing walk.
- **A15 (G4-2) — restore judges incarnation statuses per track.** The registry restore checks (`fsm/table_registry_validation.go:225`, `:244`, `:266-291`) compare `AddBlockSeq` / `RetireBlockSeq` with the global watermark. After the activation they compare them with the published frontier of the incarnation's owner (`incarnationPublishedSeq`).
- **A16 (G4-3) — one manifest per label, deterministically.** With C6 two manifests may carry the same `safe_block_seq`. `ManifestBySafeBlock` (`fsm/reads.go:200-212`) walks from the watermark through `ParentSnapshotID` and returns the newest manifest with that label (so `GetManifestByBlock` is deterministic).
- **A17 (G4-4) — no frontiers before the activation; explicit schema checks after.** Before the activation `validateManifestPublication` refuses a manifest carrying `track_frontiers` (`track_frontiers before the tracks activation`), even on the genesis branch, because a v0.11.0 voter refuses it at decode. After the activation it checks the C1 schema root and `validateManifestSchemas` explicitly before the recomputation.
- **A18 (G4-5) — more restore checks.** `validateTrackState` also requires `Initial.IndexerID == IndexerID`, a cutover within the sealed chain and `PromotionSeq`, `RejectedParts` strictly ordered by `(block, table, partition)`, and — when `TracksEnabled` is false, whatever the container version — no header track and no open-block owner. A bootstrap carrying `tracks_enabled` is refused by `validateConsensusHistory` (`tracks_enabled is set only by a consensus update, not at genesis`).
- **A19 (G6a-1) — the grouper pipelines its proposals.** It hands each held command to Raft through `submitTracked` in order and lets each handler wait through `awaitTracked` (the two halves of `proposeTracked`, `server/server.go:241-271`), so a window's statements are enqueued back to back instead of each waiting a full commit.
- **A20 (G6a-2, G6a-3) — seal-loop details keep pre-activation behaviour.** The transition loop's bound stays 2 before the activation and is `len(si_indexers) + 1` after it; seal times are taken from `EventBlockSealed` only after the activation (snapshot-query seals keep today's metric before it).
- **A21 (G6a-4) — a narrow block read.** `(f *FSM) TrackBlocks(id, after, through uint64) []uint64` lists the blocks of track `id` in `(after, through]` for publication metrics; `L3BlockView` (which copies every envelope) is not used for it.
- **A22 (G6a-5) — leadership read and server shutdown.** `raftnode.Node.IsLeader()` and `(*server.Server).Close()` are new; `raftnode/node.go`, `raftnode/node_test.go` and `cmd/arbiter/app.go` belong to Task 13.
- **A23 (G6a-6, G6b-1) — `consensus show` needs the server copy, once.** `server/consensus_admin.go` builds `ConsensusMutableParams` field by field, so `TracksEnabled` must be copied there; §3.9's "no code change" applies to `arbiter-admin` only. Task 6 makes that one-line change together with its test (it is the only edit under `server/` outside Task 13); Task 13 does not repeat it.
- **A24 (G6a facts) — the publish tail.** Task 9 keeps `publishManifest`'s `previousSafe` read, its `observePublishedBlocks` call and the `safe watermark advanced` log line; Task 13 replaces that tail for the per-track observation. Every `*Locked` helper Tasks 6–8 add is a pure read, so Task 13 may call it under the read lock. Task 13 owns every other change under `server/`.
- **A25 (G6b-2) — the grouping window's config field.** `config.IngressConfig.SubmissionGroupingWindow config.Duration` (YAML `ingress.submission_grouping_window`).
- **A26 (G6b-4) — the drain gate's refusal texts.** After the activation the drain gate keeps the three stage-1 texts and adds `consensus update requires all rejected-part cleanups to be acknowledged`.
- **A27 (fixture reconciliation) — two fixtures, two numberings.** Task 6's shared fixture `tracksFSM(t)` enrols the second indexer as id 0 (SNode `s0`, table `db0.x`) so every track test also exercises indexer 0. Tasks 10–11 were drafted against stage 1's `ownerFSMWithAuthority` numbering (indexer 2, SNode `s2`, table `db2.x`), so Task 10 defines its own `tracksFSMQ(t)` — `ownerFSMWithAuthority` plus the tracks activation — in `fsm/quarantine_fixture_test.go`, and Tasks 10–11 use it; Task 9's `tmFixture` is likewise its own. The orchestrator test helpers `authorityContextO` and `applyTracksUpdateO` are defined once, by Task 11 (`orchestrator/rejected_cleanup_test.go`), and reused by Task 13.
- **A28 (G3-1) — no capability raise in or after the activation.** The capability rule of §3.1 is judged on the params `verifyConsensusTransition` returns: an update whose resulting params have `TracksEnabled` and a higher `artifact_disposition_capability` than before is refused (`artifact disposition capability cannot be raised while tracks are enabled`), which also covers an activation update that would raise it.
- **A29 (G3-3) — per-owner grouping is a new function.** `pendingTableSetChangesLocked` keeps its signature (`fsm/table_set_transition_plan_test.go:35` calls it); the per-owner grouping is `pendingTableSetChangesByOwnerLocked`, and the per-owner plan is `plannedTrackTransitionLocked`.
- **A30 (G3-4) — the frontier of a track without a later block.** `trackPromotionFrontierLocked(id)` is the first block of track `id` above its prefix, or the prefix itself when there is none (spec §7.2); `promotionTrackLocked` resolves through `sharedTrackLocked`, and `trackPromotionRefusalLocked` holds the three per-track issuance refusals in contract order. Tasks 8 and 9 ship in the same arbiter release (the no-release window of the Global Constraints): before Task 9 a track's published frontier never leaves its `Initial`.
- **A31 (PR #234 review, finding 1) — the leader probes every voter itself.** Spec §7.6 makes the leader refuse the tracks activation unless every voter passes the capability probe; the CLI's probe is only a preflight. `arbiter-admin consensus update --tracks-enabled` forwards its `--voter` admin addresses in gRPC metadata `arbiter-tracks-voters` (comma-separated, the `arbiter-evict-unnamed` pattern). The leader's `tracksGate` (Task 13), under the same `membershipMu` lock and read barrier, dials each named address (insecure gRPC, like `arbiter-admin`), calls `GetProtocolInfo` with a bounded timeout, and requires the set of returned `node_id`s to equal the raft voter set exactly and every returned `features` list to contain `track_manifests_v1`. A request without the metadata, an unreachable or duplicate address, a node id outside the voter set, a missing voter, or a voter without the feature refuses the update with `FailedPrecondition` before anything is proposed (`tracks gate refused: ...`, naming the offending voter). Tests (Task 13): a direct-RPC server test with one stage-1 voter (features without `track_manifests_v1`) asserts the refusal and that no proposal reached Raft; a missing-voter test; a foreign-node-id test; a no-metadata test. Task 14's CLI sends the metadata and keeps its own probe as a preflight.
- **A32 (PR #234 review, finding 2) — a released track stays refused on its host until its rejected parts are cleaned.** Clearing `Quarantined` at release would let the host serve `unsafe_latest` reads of rejected candidate rows that are still in `hg_unsafe` until their asynchronous cleanup is acknowledged. `TableRegistryView.QuarantinedIndexers` (served as `TableRegistrySnapshot.quarantined_indexers`) therefore lists every indexer that is quarantined or still holds a `RejectedPartition` (draining). Task 10's `quarantinedIndexersLocked` computes it that way; Task 11 bumps the registry once when the last rejected partition of a track is acknowledged. The FSM admits the released track's statements at once (admission reads only the `Quarantined` flag); its host keeps answering Refused for reads and writes until the view drops it. `GetTrackState.quarantined` stays the FSM flag. The proto comment of `quarantined_indexers` says "quarantined, or released with rejected parts not yet cleaned"; sentio-node's `quarantined` info field means the same (Task 16 documents it). Test (Task 11): `TestReleasedTrackStaysInTheQuarantinedViewUntilItsRejectedPartsAreCleaned` — the view lists the track after the release, drops it after the last acknowledgement, with exactly one registry bump at each step.
- **A33 (PR #234 review, finding 3) — restore authenticates scheduled rejected cleanups.** Task 12: `validateTrackState` requires every `RejectedPartition` with `Scheduled != nil` to carry exactly `UnsafeCleanup{TableID, PartitionID, PromotionSeq: 0, RejectedBlockSeq: BlockSeq, Parts}`, and every unscheduled one to have an empty `AuthorityJWS` and a zero `AuthorityEpoch`. `validateConsensusHistory` (which holds the per-epoch params) verifies each scheduled partition's `AuthorityJWS` over `authority.CleanupCommandHash(*Scheduled)` with `verifyAuthorityContext` under `paramsByEpoch[AuthorityEpoch]`, and requires `tracksWorkEpochFloor <= AuthorityEpoch <= ConsensusEpoch` (A7). Restore-tamper tests: the scheduled command, its parts, an epoch below the floor and above the current epoch, the JWS, and proof fields on an unscheduled entry.
- **A34 (PR #234 review, finding 4) — restore re-checks every track frontier.** Task 12's `validateRestoredTrackManifest` checks, for every track-aware manifest of the restored chain: entries strictly ascending and naming enrolled indexers only; each entry at least its indexer's `Initial` on both fields and `SafeBlockSeq >= Cutover.BlockSeq`; against the parent, every parent entry still present with both fields at least the parent's (no removal, no regression) and at least one entry advanced; each entry's `SafeBlockSeq` at least the track's last block at or below the manifest's `safe_block_seq`; `AppliedPromotionSeq <= PromotionSeq`; and the first track-aware manifest names every indexer whose `Initial` equals the cutover. Exact membership at later publications (an indexer enrolled between two publications) is enforced by the live validator when each manifest is published, because the state does not record when an enrolment happened relative to a publication. Restore-tamper tests for each rule.
- **A35 (PR #234 second review) — restore binds every track cutoff to the manifest's tables.** A34's monotonicity checks do not stop a rewritten snapshot from raising a carried track's `applied_promotion_seq` while its tables still omit that track's newer promotions (a Spec D replica would then skip them), nor from lowering it while the tables already hold their effects. The state cannot tell an applied promotion from one consumed by `Applied:false` (both only set `Acked`), so Task 12 adds `PendingPromotion.Applied bool `json:"applied,omitempty"``, set by `applyRecordPromotionAck` for an `Applied:true` acknowledgement only after the tracks activation (pre-activation bytes unchanged; restore refuses it in a pre-v20 container and on a promotion issued at or before `Cutover.PromotionSeq`). `validateRestoredTrackManifest` then checks, for every track-aware manifest M and every promotion P of track T issued after the cutover (`seq > Cutover.PromotionSeq`, T from `promotionTrackLocked`), with c = M's entry for T: if `P.seq <= c`, P is acknowledged, and when `P.Applied` every candidate part of P is listed by `part_row_lthash` in M's `active_parts` of P's table and partition (unless M no longer holds that table); if `P.seq > c`, none of P's candidate parts is listed in M. Restore-tamper tests raise a carried track's cutoff without adding its promotions' parts, and lower an advanced track's cutoff below a promotion its tables reflect; both are refused.

### Tasks 10–11 (G5)

#### Contract conflicts

- G5-1: Restore refuses a quarantined track's suspended work once a consensus update has passed the drain gate. Contract §3.5 lets an update pass while a quarantined track holds an unacknowledged promotion or a pending cleanup, and Review Focus 4–5 require that state; every applied update increments `ConsensusEpoch` (`arbiter:fsm/consensus_updates.go:141`). `validateConsensusHistory` refuses exactly that state — `arbiter:fsm/consensus_history.go:75-77` (`snapshot pending promotion %d belongs to a drained authority epoch`) and `:132-134` (`snapshot pending cleanup %d belongs to a drained authority epoch`) — on every `Restore`, `ConfigureGenesis` and `ValidateGenesis` (`arbiter:fsm/genesis_validation.go:68`, `arbiter:fsm/snapshot.go:691`), and §3.7 does not relax it, so after the first such update no snapshot would restore (node restart, `InstallSnapshot`). Proposed amendment (append to contract §3.5): "Restore (`validateConsensusHistory`) keeps the drained-epoch refusal for work issued before the tracks activation and accepts an unacknowledged promotion or a pending cleanup whose authority epoch is at or after `tracksWorkEpochFloor(paramsByEpoch)`, the first epoch whose parameters carry `tracks_enabled`. Task 12's `validateTrackState` applies the same floor to a scheduled `RejectedPartition` and verifies its `AuthorityJWS` with `authority.CleanupCommandHash(*Scheduled)` under the parameters of its `AuthorityEpoch`." Affected steps: Task 10 Steps 5–8 (`TestHistoryAcceptsQuarantinedWorkFromAnEarlierEpoch`, `TestTracksWorkEpochFloor`, the `fsm/consensus_history.go` edit); Task 12 (`validateTrackState`).
- G5-2: A quarantine without a reason. Contract §3.7 makes restore refuse a quarantined track whose reason is empty, but §3.5 gives Apply no rule refusing an empty `reason` (only the RPC's shape check, §3.8), so a command that reaches the log by any other path commits state that restore refuses (`arbiter-core:authority/evict_node.go:24-26`, which Task 4 copies, refuses an empty reason only inside the hash, with a different message). Proposed amendment (§3.5, Quarantine): "refused when `strings.TrimSpace(reason)` is empty (`quarantine indexer <id>: reason must be non-empty`), checked after the si_indexers entry and before the authority token." Affected steps: Task 10 Steps 1–3 (`TestQuarantineCommandsNeedTheCurrentAuthorityContext/no reason`, `applyQuarantineIndexer`); Task 14 (`--reason` required).
- G5-3: Unnamed refusals of the quarantine commands. §3.5 fixes only `quarantine requires the tracks activation`, the generation refusal and the release-list refusal, while Task 13 returns every FSM `Rejected` reason to the operator as `FailedPrecondition` and Task 14 prints it. Proposed amendment (§3.5): "`indexer <id> is not an si_indexers entry`; `<quarantine|release> indexer <id>: authority: <err>`; `indexer <id> is already quarantined`; `indexer <id> is not quarantined`; in `release must acknowledge exactly the rejected blocks <list>`, `<list>` is Go `%v` of the track's `Rejected` (`[]` when empty), and the comparison is with the list as committed, not its canonical form; `QuarantineIndexer`/`ReleaseIndexer` share `quarantine requires the tracks activation`." Affected steps: Task 10 Steps 1–3.
- G5-4: Unnamed rules and refusals of the rejected-part cleanup. §3.5–§3.6 do not say how Apply treats an acknowledgement carrying `rejected_block_seq` before the activation (§0 makes only the gateway refuse it, yet a stage-1 voter refuses it at decode), an acknowledgement with `promotion_seq != 0`, an acknowledgement for a recorded partition that was never scheduled, a rejected block whose statement list is incomplete at release (`arbiter:fsm/apply.go:182-200`), nor what the drain gate says for a rejected partition. Proposed amendment (§3.6): "Apply refuses a cleanup or an acknowledgement carrying `rejected_block_seq` before the tracks activation, first, with `rejected-part cleanup requires the tracks activation`; it refuses `rejected-part cleanup must carry promotion_seq 0` (cleanup) and `rejected-part cleanup ack must carry promotion_seq 0` (acknowledgement); schedule refusals are `schedule cleanup: no rejected parts of block <b> are recorded in <table>/<partition>` and `schedule cleanup: the parts differ from the rejected parts of block <b> in <table>/<partition>`; an acknowledgement for a partition that is recorded but not scheduled is refused (`cleanup ack: the rejected parts of block <b> in <table>/<partition> are not scheduled`) and one for a partition that is not recorded is an idempotent no-op; a release computes its rejected partitions before its first mutation and refuses with `release indexer <id>: block <b> is unknown or incomplete` when a block's statement list is incomplete; the drain gate refuses with `consensus update requires all rejected-part cleanups to be acknowledged`. Rejected partitions never enter `PendingCleanups` or `CleanupAudits`, which are keyed by promotion sequence." Affected steps: Task 11 Steps 1–4.

### Task 13 (G6a)

#### Contract conflicts
- G6a-1: §3.8 grouping window, "at close it proposes the held commands from one goroutine through the existing `proposeTracked` … and hands each handler its own result" — `proposeTracked` (`server/server.go:241-271`) returns only after `waitApply` saw the command apply, so a window's statements proposed one after another through it would each wait a full commit round before the next is even enqueued; today concurrent handlers pipeline and the Raft leader group-commits up to `MaxAppendEntries` (64) futures per dispatch (hashicorp/raft v1.7.3 `raft.go:905-932`, digest §1.4), so the literal rule caps a leader at one statement per commit latency — proposed amendment: "at close it hands the held commands to Raft from one goroutine through `submitTracked` (`proposeTracked`'s first half: encode and `Node.Apply`, in owner order, which fixes the log order), and each handler awaits its own future through `awaitTracked` (`proposeTracked`'s second half); `proposeTracked` is the two halves in sequence and unchanged for every other caller". Affected: Task 13 Step 11 (drafted per amendment A19 (proposed as G6a-1)).
- G6a-2: §3.8 seal loop, "bounded by the number of enrolled indexers plus one per pass" — read literally the bound is 1 on a network without `si_indexers` and therefore cuts today's drain-then-transition pair (`orchestrator/seal.go:68-69`, `attempt < 2`), a pre-activation behaviour change — proposed amendment: "after the tracks activation the transition branch repeats … bounded by the number of enrolled indexers plus one per pass; before it the pass keeps today's two proposals". Affected: Step 7 (per amendment A23 (proposed as G6a-6)).

### Tasks 14–15 (G6b)

#### Contract conflicts

- **G6b-1: nothing copies `Params.TracksEnabled` into `ConsensusMutableParams`.** Contract §3.9 says `consensus show` needs no code change and that every CLI update carries `tracks_enabled` once set, which both read `GetConsensusParams().current.tracks_enabled`. But `server/consensus_admin.go:69-83` (`consensusMutableParams`) copies each field by name (authority addresses, `max_writers`, capability, registry, lanes, `si_indexers`, `verifiers`), and neither contract §3.1 (Task 6) nor §3.8 (Task 13) adds `TracksEnabled`. Without it `consensus show` reports false forever, every CLI update after the activation drops the field (the FSM refuses: `consensus update must carry tracks_enabled once set`), and the CLI would run the activation gate again (refused by its track-state check). Proposed amendment (contract §3.1, Task 6): "In the commit that adds `Params.TracksEnabled`, `server/consensus_admin.go` `consensusMutableParams` sets `TracksEnabled: p.TracksEnabled` (`pb.ConsensusMutableParams.tracks_enabled = 8`), with a server test that `GetConsensusParams` reports it in `current` after the activation and never in `bootstrap`." Affected steps: Task 14 Steps 3–4 (the carry and the gate trigger; `TestCLITracksActivationQuarantineAndReleaseThroughServerAndFSM` asserts `consensus show` reports it), Task 15 Step 3 (`tracksCluster.update` carries it). Cross-check against the parallel drafts: both the Task 6 draft (`g3-t06-08.md`, Files: `server/consensus_admin.go:74-82`) and the Task 13 draft (`g6a-t13.md`, its conflict G6a-6, which says Task 6 must not edit `server/`) add this line; the assembled plan must give it to exactly one of them.
- **G6b-2: the grouping window's Go config field is not named.** Contract §3.8 fixes the YAML key `ingress.submission_grouping_window` and `server.Config.SubmissionGroupingWindow`, not the `config` field. Task 15 forwards it in `integration/cluster_node_test.go` `newServices` as `cfg.Ingress.SubmissionGroupingWindow.Duration`, beside `IngressConfig.MaxStatementAge` (`config/config.go:52-55`), and sets it with `withSubmissionGroupingWindow`. Proposed amendment (contract §3.8, Grouping window): "Config: `config.IngressConfig.SubmissionGroupingWindow config.Duration` (YAML `submission_grouping_window`; raw pointer default `50ms`; …)". Affected steps: Task 15 Step 3. Cross-check: the parallel Task 13 draft (`g6a-t13.md`, Produces) uses exactly this field.
- **G6b-3: a per-track stall alert cannot tell an idle track from a stuck one.** The README must show "a per-track alert example on `arbiter_track_safe_block_seq`", but with contract §3.8's four gauges a track's prefix stays put both when its indexer writes nothing and when its next block is stuck; no gauge exposes a track's pending blocks. Task 14's `ArbiterTrackStalled` therefore also matches tracks without writes, and the README says so and how to narrow it (an `indexer_id` matcher, `consensus tracks`, `GetL3Block`'s `track`). Proposed amendment (optional; no S2-A change needed): a later release adds `arbiter_track_pending_blocks{indexer_id}` (sealed blocks of the track above its prefix) and the rule requires it above 0. Affected steps: Task 14 Step 5 (README text only).
- **G6b-4: the drain gate's refusal texts after the activation are not fixed.** Contract §3.5 changes which work counts (quarantined tracks are skipped, rejected partitions count) but names no text. Task 15 matches the stage-1 texts (`consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged`, `… all cleanup commands to be acknowledged`, `… all promoted unsafe parts to be cleaned`, `fsm/consensus_updates.go:74-88`) and `waitUpdate` retries on the prefix `consensus update requires all`. Proposed amendment (contract §3.5, Drain gate): "The three stage-1 refusal texts are kept; an unacknowledged rejected partition of a track that is not quarantined refuses with `consensus update requires all rejected-part cleanups to be acknowledged`." Affected steps: Task 15 Steps 1 and 3 (if Task 10 or 11 chose another text for rejected partitions, `waitUpdate`'s prefix check must follow it). Cross-check: the parallel Tasks 10–11 draft (`g5-t10-11.md`) uses exactly this text, which `waitUpdate`'s prefix covers.
